Chapter 16: To Be A Sister (Arc 2, Part 11)
Chapter Summary

Rem's memories continue. It's awfully confusing at times.

Chapter Notes

Okay, here we go! I hope you enjoy!

(We're on track for the demonic Arc 2 to be 13 chapters total, by the way. Which means
that after this, there should be two chapters left!)

See the end of the chapter for more notes

["Are you alright?” Ram asked. “Is the abundance of people too much for you to
handle? I guess it's expected. After all, it is your first time being somewhere with this
many people."]

 

Rem frowned, glancing over the scenery in front of her. It looked familiar. “This is…”

 

“The Capital of Lugunica,” Ram confirmed quietly. “It’s where we watched Subaru — deal
with the Bowel Hunter situation, before he came to the Manor.”

 

Rem nodded slowly.

 

—Frederica suddenly had a thought. Was this the twins’ first time visiting the Capital?

 

Something very strange had gone down, the day that Ram had visited the Capital for the very
first time. She couldn’t remember it all that clearly, but perhaps that was because…

 



["Nee-sama, sorry for making you worried,” Rem said, placing a hand over where Ram
has reached over to worriedly caress her cheek. “I'm fine."]

 

[“Are you sure?” Ram pressed. “You don't have to push yourself, If you can't do it, then
you can wait in the dragon carriage quietly…”]

 

["No really, I'm fine. I can't be disheartened from something like this."]

 

Hetaro’s face twisted. Knowing what Rem had decided behind her older sister’s back, and
then seeing Ram caring for her just like an older sibling should…! Did Rem really just —
never realize what she would be doing to Ram, with a decision like that?

 

“Onii-chan,” Tivey hissed, his arm being clenched tight by his older brother. “Onii-chan,
you’re hurting me…!”

 

Hetaro suddenly remembered the story of The Red Oni Who Cried, and his face twisted even
further.

 

Tivey yelped. “Onii-chan—!”

 

["How's your first time being at the Royal Capital?” Roswaal asked. “It's preeeetty
splendid, right?"]

 

Frederica frowned even further. So it was, then.

 

["You two, please be very careful so that you don't get lost,” Frederica warned.
“Finding a lost child in this city is no simple task. It's very difficult."]

 

Subaru snorted. Emilia placed a hand over her mouth to hide her giggle. Both of them were
thinking of the same young daughter of the Appa seller, whom they had each stopped to help
on the busy streets of that very place.



 

“—Oh,” Ram said. “I remember this.”

 

Rem blinked. “Nee-sama?”

 

“We were there to find a gift to celebrate the new baby of the Miload family,” Frederica was
explaining across the room. “Lady Grace was…” She halted, and then continued tactfully.
“That baby would grow up to be young Annerose, of course.”

 

["For you to go through the trouble going to the Royal Capital for that, you must have a
lot of spare time,” Ram noted.]

 

["I'm giving a gift to a close friend,” Roswaal returned. “Of course I'd find the time to
choose one myself."]

 

Ram frowned. His reasoning had been a little more complicated than that: she remembered
that much.

 

Though, he and Grace had been close. So perhaps there was a bit of truth to that statement,
after all.

 

She shook her head. “It was for the Tammuz Festival,” she continued explaining to her little
sister. “In that area, it marks the time of year when ice season ends and flowers and fruits
begin to come into season. Lord Roswaal chose to look for a present then, because rare things
appear on the market during that time that normally don’t during the rest of the year.”

 

["If you're going to be giving a present,” Roswaal declared, “you might as well make it
a special one."]

 

Anastasia smiled. She herself had gone by the same rules, after all, when picking out “gifts”
for the other Camps in preparation for their arrivals in Priestella. “If you’re going to give



someone a gift, you might as well give them the best gift that you can.”

 

The Margrave really was turning out to be much more sensible than she had assumed, wasn’t
he?

 

[“…The gift isn't for Lady Grace?" Frederica was clarifying.]

 

["A gift for Grace would be a present for the Miload family,” Roswaal explained. “This
is something I want to give to celebrate the baby. That's the plan."]

 

Crusch blinked. “I see,” she murmured.

 

Felt frowned. “What kinda things would a baby like?” she asked. “All they do is sit there and
make a racket all day long, they’re not gonna appreciate shit.”

 

“That’s not really accurate, Lady Felt,” Reinhard said.

 

["So you want to choose something the baby will like even though it hasn't been born
yet,” Rem said. “You sure are asking for quite the feat."]

 

["Right? It is going to be veeeery difficult. After all, I am famous for not being able to
understand feelings even with those whom I talk with face to faaaace."]

 

["That's not something you should be proud of,” Ram answered.]

 

Wilhelm chuckled slightly. It seemed as though some traits of that man’s had been inherited
from his grandmother: Roswaal J. Mathers had been infamous for her tactlessness and
outrageousness.

 



Well. That entire family was something else, in a number of ways.

 

["We'll decide on a time and place to meet, and we'll split into two groups to find a
present,” Roswaal declared. “—A present suitable for a soon to be born child. There
will be a prize for the one that does a good jooooob."]

 

Old Man Rom huffed, crossing his arms with a soft sort of look on his face. “Didn’t expect
the Margrave to have a soft spot for young-uns,” he commented.

 

“I think he’s doing an alright job,” Ricardo grinned. Aside from…

 

Well. It had been a great benefit to Rem, in the end. So perhaps that much could be forgiven.

 

—Ram frowned. They had called off the competition early due to unforeseen circumstances,
she remembered that much. …But at least for herself, there had been a prize, all right.

 

["As long as Roswaal-sama or Frederica-sama goes alone, we can be divided into a
three-man group,” Rem was saying. “With me and Nee-sama, and a one-man group…”]

 

["You're being pretty absurd!” Frederica exclaimed. “I'll be lonely if I have to go
alone!"]

 

Garfiel chuckled. “You really are honest, eh, sis?”

 

“And those two are certainly mischievous,” Frederica muttered.

 

[“—Thank goodness,” Frederica murmured to herself.]

 

The theater quieted.



 

[Rem blinked. "Frederica-sama?"]

 

["It looks like this trip to the Capital has allowed you to relax a bit,” Frederica smiled.
“That makes me feel relieved. I was worried about your recent behavior. …I wasn't sure
how much the incident of the enemy sneaking into the basement warehouse scarred
you."]

 

Frederica blinked. “—Scarred you?” she echoed.

 

Of course, that would be partially her concern. But she would imagine that her old self would
have also been worried about…

 

[She’s not aware of the details, Rem noted. Only Roswaal-sama, Nee-sama, and I know
about the man’s background as a witch cultist, and Clind was the only one who knew
about the man’s existence.]

 

…Ah. So, Frederica had never been told about what had really happened at all.

 

She clenched her fists in her lap, and tried not to feel betrayed. It would only have frightened
her, she knew. Keeping it from her had been the intelligent decision. Perhaps even the
responsible one.

 

—Rem glanced at Frederica from across the room. The forced smile on her face made her
stomach twist into knots of guilt. Even if she didn’t remember it…

 

Ram hissed softly between her teeth. Perhaps she would need to apologize to her coworker
properly. Once all of — this — had been taken care of.

 

["Thank you for worrying about me,” Rem decided. “But I'm fine."]

 



["I can't just be convinced with that when I see those injuries. Ram's face was burning
red in anger…” Frederica curled her lip. “All of it happened because Clind had bad
timing…!"]

 

It had been a bit more than bad timing, Otto thought darkly. That cryptic order, no doubt
given from Roswaal through his eldest servant…

 

Well. That was a matter for another time, he guessed.

 

["It's true that Clind-sama had bad timing,” Rem answered carefully. “But he is the one
who found me worn-out. Besides, Roswaal is teaching me magic now, and so even if
something like that happens again, I'll be able to heal my wounds."]

 

["Please don't say that it'll happen again,” Frederica muttered. “There's no need for an
omen like that."]

 

Frederica twitched. Rem’s healing magic had taken on a decidedly twisted sort of meaning, in
her mind. —Healing magic as a form of torture was something that she never would have
dreamed of, she was certain, and yet Rem had come up with the idea all on her own when she
had been just a little girl.

 

[“A gift, something the receiver would be happy with…” Rem recited. “When I think
about it like that, it feels really difficult." Three hours had gone by, and yet…]

 

["It really does, huh,” Frederica agreed. “Rem, if, for example, Ram was going to give a
present to you, what would make you happy?"]

 

[“The fact that Nee-sama is willing to give me a gift would make me happy."]

 

Tivey scoffed. Even he would want a proper gift from Mimi, really. Hetaro, who thought
similarly to Rem, sensed what his little brother was thinking and swatted him over the head.



 

["That was a bad example,” Frederica noted. “Hmm, let's see... Switching places, what
would you give Ram? To your precious twin sister."]

 

Crusch stifled a laugh. What a poor question to ask.

 

“Well,” Wilhelm said tactfully. “Perhaps young Frederica didn’t actually want to get anything
done that day after all…”

 

[If I was going to give her a gift, what would I…? Rem wondered. The village didn’t really
deal in money, so I’d only give her things like corollas and steamed tatoes before—]

 

["But now that I'm being paid,” Rem realized. “I can give Nee-sama presents…!”]

 

“And there it is!” Felt cackled.

 

["Rem? Hey, Rem.” Frederica was prodding a shell-shocked Rem. “Are you listening to
me? Reeemmm, I shouldn't have aaasked."]

 

[“Sorry, Frederica-sama. I have to find a present for Nee-sama now!"]

 

["I admit that it's all my fault for asking! Sit down! Please sit down!"]

 

“Oh, hush,” Frederica muttered at Garfiel’s laughter. Across the theater, Rem’s cheeks were a
similar shade of red. Ram stifled a giggle of her own at the sight.

 

Emilia smiled tenderly. It was really wonderful, for someone to be so very excited at the
prospect of giving the person they loved a gift. Really, really wonderful…

 



["We're going to find a gift that will let the baby know that we wish for it to grow up
into a healthy and graceful woman,” Frederica declared.]

 

["But we don't know for sure that it's a girl, since it hasn't been born yet,” Rem pointed
out.]

 

In the present moment, Frederica preened. She had been correct in the end.

 

(She had been so selfishly happy, when she had heard that Annerose was a little girl. A little
sister-like figure was someone that Frederica had felt would be much less trouble to connect
with, as opposed to if she had been born a little boy.)

 

[Out of nowhere—]

 

“—Rem?” Subaru asked. His worried eyes were fixed upon her frozen place.

 

[That stink, Rem thought. She had frozen in place.]

 

“Oh,” Anastasia muttered.

 

“Oh no,” Crusch hissed.

 

[The same terrible stink that had filled the basement warehouse…!]

 

Garfiel’s eyes widened. “Here?!” he demanded. “Here— Now—?!”

 

Almost back to back encounters with the ones who— What kind of rotten luck was that?!

 



[“Rem?” her onscreen self asked, noticing that the young girl had inexplicably stopped
in the middle of the street. “What’s wrong?”]

 

Ah. Frederica exhaled. So that really had…

 

[Rem turned towards the alley where the stench was coming from, and then she broke
into a sprint.]

 

[“Rem—?!” Frederica cried.]

 

[Rem wasn’t listening. Her mind was fixated on one thing and one thing only: This is the
evil scent that deserves to be punished—!]

 

Frederica couldn’t remember the details very clearly. But she knew that something had
happened, that day at the festival.

 

“—You didn’t even think to say anything first?” she murmured, watching as Rem left behind
her bewildered self. “Instead, you immediately…”

 

But Rem had always been a reckless sort of girl, hadn’t she?

No, it won’t. Ram crossed her arms, lifting her chin high. It hadn’t then, and that worthless

That was the voice of an older sister, Mimi understood. She gripped her two little brothers

Mimi punched the air, a cheerful sort of triumph in her howl.

The sight of it— The sight of power, of determination, of the golden glow of the sun, of

She had been the one responsible for fixing it, after all.

Taking a heavy burden like that into himself… But, such was the duty of the Lord of the

In the present moment, Rem startled.

Synesthesia, once again. A sort of magic between twins. —To be honest, Ferris had thought

Strong, was it? Wilhelm looked at the girls with pity. To never cry was a show of strength for

A young girl like Ram, finding herself unable to cry her own tears…

Ahh. Anastasia exhaled slowly, feeling as though something had settled into place. An excuse,

It was a shame, to see a girl afraid to be sad, to be happy, to be angry, if any of it were for the

Julius remembered hearing rumors that Lord Roswaal had been directing things from behind

Subaru watched as Rem cried, and cried, and refused to allow herself to feel her tears as her

[“Thank you so much, Master,” Clind was saying a few days later. “I have never been so

“Eh??” Rem leaned away from the screen, eyes wide. “That’s—”

 

That was some enthusiasm, all right.

 

“—Oh no,” Subaru muttered. He already knew where this was going.

 

["Your unexpected level of motivation makes me feel nothing but anxious!" Frederica

Ram sighed. “Frederica sure did have her work cut out for her, back then,” she murmured.

["But…”]

Well. It was kind of fun, to know that something as fantastical as that had been living right

So the two of them HAD formed a good relationship after all, had they? Just like she was

Perhaps she had been rather foolish to ever doubt such a thing. Frederica almost wanted to

…Well.

 

Garfiel’s eyes softened at the sight of his sister’s joyful face. He had never understood that

She didn’t have any real memories of this place, and she had no attachment to it either. Even

…Was that how it worked? Rem wasn’t really sure.

 

["Nee-sama, let's hold hands."]

Felt huffed, smiling a little bit in spite of herself. Rem was a real sap sometimes, wasn’t she?

 

Subaru began to smile weakly. He didn’t really — want to see this place again, not after

Subaru’s face soured.

 

It wasn’t like he could ever be grateful, when it came to something as awful as that fiery

Crusch exhaled slowly. It was thanks to that tragedy that Rem had gotten to the point where

Old Man Rom smiled sadly. Setanta, you old fool…

["…Ah."]

Likely not — especially not if Anastasia’s suspicions about the true extent of the Margrave’s

Lord Roswaal seemed like a Master who took good care of the things that belonged to him,

Wilhelm nodded solemnly. With retribution achieved, the dead would be able to rest soundly.

[Then she passed Rem the remaining alcohol, and politely moved away so that Rem

A promise she would never break. Emilia tilted her head. So, Rem had been the type to care

“Ah…” Tivey winced.

Hetaro hissed, shrinking backwards in his seat. Mimi’s face darkened significantly.

 

If anyone were ever — EVER — to make the little siblings of the Pearlbaton triplets feel like

Reinhard smiled sadly. That was the truth of the matter, wasn’t it? As painful as it might be,

(A certain sense of kinship bloomed in his heart. The feeling was so rare for him that he

Julius swallowed.

 

It wasn’t the same situation, but there was a certain resemblance, here, to his adoption into

A girl who would walk in the light, so that she could lead her sister along behind her. Otto

—Well. That had been that way for a long time, hadn’t it?

Subaru watched as Rem’s clock slowed to a stop before his very eyes, and he could almost

These people, these complications, this reality full of disgusting things that they all were

If it were up to Anastasia, what would she consider the best way to utilize all of it? What

He really had looked pathetic, hadn’t he? Subaru stared at his old self, moaning and

Frederica’s eyes were soft as she watched her coworkers stay by Subaru’s side. This…

 

Yes. Frederica could recognize these two women who could have been her coworkers.

 

—It was kinda gross, wasn’t it?

 

Garfiel stared at the two sisters performing that act of genuine kindness, and realized that he

Nowadays, Beatrice was the one to hold Subaru’s hand when he had a nightmare. Part of her

[The next day, Rem went to the village to shop for supplies. There were a couple of

(Crusch watched Ferris with a worried, wary expression. She thanked the spirits for the

No need for any other relationships… Ricardo grimaced. That was — a very bad way to view

That mindset felt worse and worse the more he thought about it.

There was nothing remotely amusing about this. It was just painful.

It really was a sloppy sort of cover-up. Errors like this would surely only have made him

["You all right?” Subaru asked, face almost frantic with eagerness. “You're so swamped

“Ah,” Crusch murmured. “Rem is…”

[Faster than she could call out to stop him, Subaru rushed down the hallway and out of

Beatrice swallowed. It stung more than it should, perhaps, to see Subaru running away from

It was a bitter sort of reassurance, but at least the boy had some self-preservation instincts.

[Rem relaxed a little, after that afternoon — but only just a little bit. The moment in the

That was very accurate. Anastasia was somewhat ashamed to admit it, but the first time she

Reinhard chuckled. Where Subaru’s value was concerned, his technical skills were perhaps

Emilia’s eyes softened. “Oh, Rem…”

[Subaru-kun is still a troublesome interloper, Rem thought reluctantly, watching him on

Ram — relaxed. Just a little bit.

 

Old Man Rom chuckled. Rem had never been the type to welcome any changes to her

It sounded like an exaggeration. Perhaps it was. But to wipe out a village’s children — would

[Rem’s breath caught in her throat when she heard about the missing children, and saw

[Why would someone so powerless act so desperately for children he barely knows?! Rem

—Or perhaps her old self had been able to recognize something that flew in the face of that

It was an unusual trait indeed. Otto had come to admire that easy selfless heroism in both

“That’s not arrogance.”

 

Anastasia’s sudden declaration was so harsh that it made the people around her flinch. Her

“It’s not,” she repeated, forcefully softening her tone. “Relying on others to provide for what

Her younger self, a little girl in Kararagi who hadn’t food, or clothes, or shelter, or even a

Before, Rem had trembled with every strike of that morningstar. Now the impact still sent

Garfiel knew the strength of demihuman blood, the overwhelming nature of instincts running

Wilhelm didn’t feel much of anything, watching Rem’s bloodthirsty rampage through the

Crusch pressed her lips together, silently agreeing. Though, she did have to admit: Rem’s

She could have saved him, Mimi understood. Rem could have saved that boy, but she

What would it take, for Tivey to think something like that about either of his big siblings? He

With how that Clan had treated the two of them, way back then, Rom thought grimly. It was

How could someone like— Someone that— Someone who served, who supported, who

A person should live in a way that allows their soul to shine its brightest. This was what

How horrible, Anastasia thought faintly. What an awful trap to ensnare oneself into, and with

Tivey blinked rapidly. “Lacking?” he repeated, with a note of disbelief.

If someone were to insist on standards like that, then everything in the world would feel like

Anything would have appeared subpar, with the Reincarnation of an Oni God as a role

It wasn’t like she was unfamiliar with the concept of atonement. She herself, after all, was

For him to not be it, for him to relinquish it, for him to vanish from it, would be for him to

[Just now, in the woods, Rem thought in despair. I committed the sin from long ago…

So, she was thinking. She felt somewhat numb. This was not because she had nothing to feel

The same thought, she had said.

 

“…What?” Rem asked, her voice meek and trembling.

 

“That night our village was attacked,” Ram answered. “When that cultist broke off my horn.
All I could think in that moment was — ‘It finally broke off.’”

 



The theater was silent. Not a soul even dared to breathe. Even the dimmest amongst them

This was a moment between sisters. None of them were allowed to intrude on it.

 

“That horn caused me more trouble than it was worth,” Ram dismissed. “And I never cared

Rem — didn’t know what to say. “…Nee-sama…?” she asked quietly.

 

In her heart of hearts, Rem knew that these were Ram’s true feelings on the matter. By now,

people’s sakes.

 

“I might…not remember you, Dear Sister,” Ram apologized, her voice unusually soft. “But I
remember that much, as clear as if it happened yesterday.” She turned away. “That burden
you took it upon yourself to carry — it was one that never really existed in the first place.”

 

Rem stared at her sister speechlessly, an odd feeling stirring within her chest. Was it grief, for
years that had been wasted on such a foolish mission? Was it shame, for a task that had been
taken on for the sake of a person who would have wanted nothing to do with it? Was it anger,
that nobody had thought to say all of these things sooner, letting them fester in the dark? Or
was it simple, plain relief?

 

—With guilt, Rem thought that those words were exactly what someone else would have
wanted to hear, at the exact time when someone else would have wanted to hear them most.

 

But that person wasn’t here anymore, because the current Rem had taken her place.

 



—The Rem of the present moment took a deep breath. “I really am blessed to be your little
sister,” she said softly. “I really do believe that, Nee-sa…” Rem blinked, and then smiled.
“Onee-chan.”

 

Ram stared at her with wide eyes, before a wonderful, wonderful smile broke over her face.
I’m blessed, too,” she said. “Very, very blessed. Never forget what a blessing you are to me in
turn, Rem — because I would do just about anything for you.”

 

And wasn’t that the truth?

 

The meteor went dark again. Then—

 

["Barusu!” Ram’s voice snapped. “Head to the right of that broken tree ahead! You're
too slow!"]

 

["Don't — demand the impossible!” Subaru’s voice responded, panting loudly. “I'm —”
He gasped for air. “I’m running — as fast as I can, here!"]

 

[The Rem onscreen slowly blinked open her eyes.]

 

The demonstration resumed.

Chapter 18: To Be You (Arc 2, Part 13)
Chapter Summary

Subaru has a couple of conversations that have, for various reasons, been long overdue.

Chapter Notes
See the end of the chapter for notes

[“…Subaru-kun,” Rem murmured blearily. “What are y—”]

 

["—Rem!” Subaru gasped. His shoulder was dislocated, the side of his face was wet

But everyone knew she wasn’t. Frederica exhaled slowly. That sort of thinking, that inability

Perhaps the dizzying effects of the Yin magic were messing with Beatrice’s head too, even as

[Why did this nothingness come? Who brought it? What are the conditions for ending it?

Frederica shivered at the very thought. To have nothing at all in the world except for the

“Come on…” Hetaro hissed.

 

Tivey gritted his teeth, balling his hands into fists. “Come on…!”

 

[I can’t make it another step. My feet are drained of all strength. Sooner or later, the

Anastasia’s eyes were stern. “Don’t give in,” she muttered. “Stand strong, Natsuki, ya can do

If he could feel the ground beneath his feet, then he could stand. If he could stand, he could

That’s right, Crusch wanted to praise him. The truth lies within. It always lies within. The

Felt could do nothing but wait with bated breath for Subaru to find himself in a world of

To find himself, so that he could finally take that step forward towards the light of victory —

[Even if I can’t bring the oblivion outside me to heel, I can call upon my internal organs,

[And with that, Subaru bit down on the bokka fruit.]

 

Even knowing that it was coming, Ferris couldn’t keep from flinching, hissing loudly in

Emilia heard the wordless, bestial cry that Subaru attempted to wail aloud in response to this

She croaked, torn between gratitude that she had happened to give him that tool for his

Yes, yes, yes…! So coiled up with tension as he was, Ricardo’s support couldn’t make it out

[Awareness, oblivion, awareness, oblivion, awareness, oblivion, over and over and over—!]

 

[—And then Subaru broke through the black cloud, and his sword thrust itself deep

“YES!” Wilhelm howled, practically leaping to his feet as he punched the air. His cry was

[I just… My sword, my hand, my…]



 

Subaru’s dazed voice, like someone who had abruptly been shocked out of their own body,

Ah. Ricardo winced, confusion and worry turning into an embarrassed sort of sympathy at

(It didn’t feel good. But blessings weren’t always pretty, he knew — and they never came

Staring at the surreal sight, Frederica had to agree.

["—Thanks a million, brats." Subaru spat out the remnants of a bokka fruit.]

[The beast roared in agony, flinging Subaru’s body away to tumble across the ground

Frederica had thought that covering her eyes would make things more tolerable, but having to

[“—Ul Goa.”]

 



[The ground in front of Subaru’s face exploded into flames.]

The theater around her bursting into cries of alarm, Ram winced. She understood that

["What the hell just…?”]

 

[And then Subaru saw the state of his opponent.]

 

“Holy shit,” Garfiel gasped. Wide-eyed next to him, Frederica was too stricken by the sight

—Of course, basically nobody would bother empathizing with such a monster. Such

(Emilia turned away. Subaru swallowed back his regrets. Nobody could tear their eyes away

“I’d say that counts as a fair bit more than just a suspension!” Crusch squeaked, her face

[Around Subaru, other flaming spells bore down from above into the black cloud that

It was mercy, Ferris knew. A quick blow, and then they wouldn’t even know it until it was

It was cruelty, Wilhelm was sure. A warrior wanted to keep their eyes open until their final

(And even outside of them being monsters, they had killed Subaru without him being aware

["Myyy, my, myyy,” a familiar voice called out, the source descending from on high

“Oh thank FUCK.”

 

Rachins didn’t even mean to exclaim it, the words just slipping out as he slumped backwards

But Roswaal had just saved Subaru from certain death. So, the two of them could allow

[And with that, Subaru lost his strength and fell to the ground, too weak to even get on

Emilia exhaled slowly. So she really had managed to help him after all.

 

She could have done more, if only Subaru had asked her to. But at least she had done this

["You sure figured out where I was, though,” Subaru was muttering.]

 

["Ah.” Roswaal smiled. “That is because of what Lady Emilia pounded iiinto me at the

Otto and Garfiel both breathed a sigh of relief, shamelessly shifting their gratitude from

—So, that was how it was.

 

Rem may have charged into those woods without a plan — but through orders to her servant

Beatrice averted her eyes. Part of her wanted to defend her efforts, but the rest of her was all

["Roswaal-sama—!" Ram’s voice shouted, and the two Oni sisters cut past the burning

Rachins snorted. “So much for escaping back to the village, huh?”

 

Before, Ram would have said something about Lord Roswaal’s side being the safest place of

["I am sorry to have caused you so much trouble,” Ram said, looking very glad to see

["Oh no, that is quite fine. Indeed, you have done veeery well in my absence."]

 

[Ram blushed at the praise, pressing a hand to her chest as she gave a solemn nod.

…Perhaps Ram would never really know what she had been thinking, back then. Not even

[“—Subaru-kun!”]

[“Gwah!” Subaru choked out, the younger sister having suddenly leapt forth to

“…Well,” Garfiel managed. “That — is certainly a shift.”

 

Frederica suddenly found herself giggling into her hand.

 

[In any other context, I’d be overjoyed, Subaru admitted inwardly. But she’s hugging me

Forcing Subaru’s hand by running impulsively off into the woods, nearly killed the boy she

Well. Perhaps Rem could just be relieved that everything had turned out alright, in the end.

“I was just sleepy!” Subaru said hastily, already seeing the theater beginning to panic at his

Old Man Rom sighed, slowly relaxing once again into his seat at the confirmation. Calling it

[Comforted by this security, Subaru finally allowed himself to fall asleep — lulled into

“I sure can’t blame you,” Julius muttered. “You did far, far more than enough, Subaru…”

 

It wasn’t that he didn’t admire it, really. But it made his stomach clench, knowing how much

[Ah… I’m back in this shadowy place again.]

 

The theater seemed to blink as one.

 

[There’s nobody here. There’s nothing here. Nothing begins. Nothing ends. A world of

“—What?” Rachins asked.

 

Mimi shrugged. “A weird dream, maybe…?”

 

“Who dreams of…this…?” Tivey muttered.

 

Hetaro smacked him upside the head. “Don’t be rude.”

 

[—Ah. She’s here.]

 

“Uh…” Felt frowned.

 

Rem swallowed. “She?” she prodded. “Wasn’t there…only the mabeast…?”

[A human silhouette. Vaguely feminine…]

 

That — didn’t exactly narrow it down. Reinhard folded his arms, trying to figure out what he

[The graze of those fingers makes me want to weep. Why do I want to weep? It’s as

Crusch felt something cold trickle down her spine. Was this…?!

 

No. No, he hadn’t tried to break… But perhaps it was.

 

She really, really hoped it wasn’t…!

 

Wilhelm shivered. He was a powerful warrior and he prided himself on his courage, but for

Ferris could only watch with a feeling of utter confusion.

Julius could only exhale slowly in something resembling relief as that — thing — faded

[“—ve you.”]

 

“Uh,” Garfiel said.

 

“…What?” Frederica asked, looking completely lost.

 

Otto didn’t say anything at all.

Garfiel had thought that he’d grown up. Really, he had: he was fifteen now and everything.

Mimi winced, hard. Children shouldn’t be anywhere near difficult things like this, and this

[“Let’s write something on Subaru’s bandages!” “Right.” “Right!” “A token of

“Annoying brats, I suppose,” Beatrice muttered.

 

“I think it’s nice, that they were able to keep their spirits up,” Reinhard said mildly. His eyes

Ferris could only watch with sad eyes. It was the burden of the compassionate, he knew, to

Crusch tentatively placed a hand on Ferris’ shoulder, and was relieved when he sank into her

Frederica exhaled slowly, remembering what Petra had confided in her about these bitter

manner after one of his more serious spells, it wouldn’t matter how young the perpetrators
were: all of them would have been swiftly and ruthlessly corrected on the spot.

 

[“Lucas!” Petra’s voice shouted. Lucas startled loudly, falling onto his rear from where
he had attempted to use Subaru as his usual climbing wall. It was the first time she had
spoken up since Subaru arrived — and in fact, she appeared to have been keeping her
distance with a worried expression — and everyone sharply turned her way. “What are
you thinking?! Subaru's only just recovered!”]

 

Julius exhaled slightly, slumping. At least one of those kids had some sense.

 



[“Oh, Petra,” Subaru blinked. “Why are you over there…?”]

 

[Petra froze.]

 

Julius frowned. “Hm?”

 

[Subaru frowned. ”What is it?”]

 

[His voice was friendly, but Petra turned away and started to run.]

 

“—Eh?!” Emilia cried, lurching forward as the theater broke into cries of surprise and slight
alarm alike. “Petra?!”

 

Ah. Crusch sighed. So, it seemed that the girl hadn’t quite gotten over the sight of Subaru’s
injuries, had she…?

 

She couldn’t blame her, of course. In fact, it was the mark of a very kind and gentle soul, to
be so affected by such a sight.

 

Rem had thought that perhaps that girl was just weaker than her peers to the sight of injury.
But if that were the case, shouldn’t seeing him up and about like this made her feel better?
Why did she still seem so…?

 

[Petra's mental state didn't seem to be a secret, nor did it seem to be unrelated to
Subaru: the way the townspeople pushed him to race after her was proof enough of
that.]

 

"Huh?" Reinhard blinked. "Why… I thought Petra didn't want to be near him?"

 



"What you want and what can be two different things, I suppose," Beatrice answered,
somewhat absentmindedly.

 

Then again, Rem thought, there was a difference between seeing an injury on its own, and
knowing that the person in question had been injured for your own sake. In a similar situation
herself, currently, Rem didn’t know if she would ever be able to fully stomach the guilt of
that particular scenario — even while knowing that the boy who had done so much for her
sake still considered it to have been entirely worth it.

 

Perhaps that knowledge even made things feel a little bit worse.

 

[“This is where things got a little messy.”]

 

[Petra startled hard, freezing for a moment before turning around to see him standing
behind her. She had apparently raced to the other side of the village: the place by the
fence where Subaru had first met the mabeast pup.]

 

Emilia stiffened slightly, seeing them both so close to the barrier. She knew that she had fixed
it by this point, and that they would be safe so long as they remained just before the line, but
still…!

 

“Reckless girl,” Beatrice sighed.

 

She normally was much more level-headed than this. Otto grimaced. It wasn’t right, seeing
Petra so out of sorts.

 

[“B-But I am too injured…” Subaru huffed dramatically, raising and lowering his
shoulders as he exaggeratedly staggered and leaned against the tree trunk. “To run as
fast as I can… Huff, I don't know if it's okay to be out sick… If you're injured… But
not sick…”]

 



Anastasia saw the magic stone hanging from the tree that he was leaning against and found
herself relaxing slightly. She had heard that the barrier had been fixed, of course, but there
was a difference between hearing it and seeing it for herself.

 

[“Why…?”]

 

[“As I thought, I can't catch my breath fast enough…” Subaru wheezed, chuckling as
he sat down. “Or, maybe I just have too little stamina.”]

 

[Petra looked bewildered, and still not amused in the slightest by his attempts at levity.]

 

[“Well, sit down, Petra.” Subaru patted the ground next to him. “Let's have a little
talk.”]

 

[“…Alright.” Looking both like she wanted to run as far as she could and like wouldn’t
be able to take her eyes off of Subaru’s face if she tried, Petra meekly sat down by his
side.]

 

Garfiel frowned. “Seriously, what’s up with her right now?”

 

Frederica sighed, watching the little girl struggle in silence through her overwhelming guilt.
Oh, Petra…

 

[“Uh, I'm not quite sure what's going on here,“ Subaru admitted. “But everyone told
me to go after you, Petra. Is there something you want to tell me?”]

 

[“O-Oh…” Petra looked distinctly uncomfortable, as if she had been set up somehow.
“Well, that's, that's true.”]

 

It really was strange to see Petra behaving so meekly. Otto grimaced. With how she normally
behaved, this was just…



 

It was unexpectedly painful, to see that strong-willed girl acting so unsure of herself.

 

[“I wonder what about,” Subaru wondered aloud, when Petra didn’t say anything else.
Then he suddenly startled, his face abruptly going pale. “Ah, maybe, did you get hurt
before I brought you out of the forest?! You might have gotten mercilessly bitten into by
those dogs, and if that left a scar…then, I'm sorry!”]

 

[Even as upset as she was, Petra seemed visibly taken aback]

 

[“The worst thing that can happen to a girl is getting a scar! Well if I recall, to prevent
scars, you gotta keep it moist or something like that…”]

 

Mimi frowned. “It is?”

 

“Well,” Anastasia giggled. “Most girls would see it that way.”

 

After all, a girl’s most prized weapon in the world was her beauty. Marring her looks would
both humiliate her soul and cripple her from moving up in the world. That was simply how it
was.

 

—Though, Ricardo thought. There were always exceptions.

 

Subaru was right about moisture being beneficial, Ferris noted. But more than that, it would
be important to keep the wound clean. Though of course, someone even semi-skilled in water
magic would likely be able to heal an injury small enough for Petra to hide it without
difficulty, in which case Rem, Beatrice, or Emilia should be capable of…

 

But that didn’t seem right, in any case. To Ferris’ eyes, Petra didn’t seem injured at all.

 



[As Subaru continued to fret, Petra looked as though she were searching for evidence of
a ploy, with a face that seemed confused by the presence of his confusion. But slowly, she
seemed to realize that Subaru was serious about both his concern and his ignorance of
what was wrong.]

 

[And with that realization followed a look of…]

 

“Angry?” Emilia asked aloud. “Petra, why are you….?”

 

[“Subaru,” Petra muttered.]

 

[“That's right! Petra, show me where you got hurt… Oh, no, I don't want to see it if it's
in a weird place…”]

 

[“—Subaru!!” Petra shouted.]

 

[“Yes, yes, yes, yes, what's wrong?” Subaru asked, spinning to face her.]

 

The look on Petra’s face made Subaru’s eyes widen even further, and it wasn’t hard to see
why. Even from this distance, Ricardo couldn’t help but cringe at the anguish emanating from
every fiber of her being. But more than just discomfort — what on Earth was making her so
upset?

 

“Getting all worked up after everything’s already been said and done…” the old kobold
sighed. He was thinking of a few more examples than just Petra. “Guess little girls are always
a handful.”

 

Anastasia sharply turned to face him, hands on her hips. “And what is THAT supposed to
mean?”

 



(Nearby, Ram could only agree — but she’d have to add that little sisters, especially, seemed
rather high-maintenance.)

 

[“S…” Petra was trembling, a mix of anger and frustration and overwhelming guilt in
her teary eyes. She appeared to be swallowing the first of those emotions, perhaps
deciding that such a reaction wasn’t appropriate for what she wanted to say in the
moment. “Sor…”]

 

[“Sor?” Subaru prodded, concerned.]

 

[“I'm sorry…!” And then Petra began to bawl in earnest.]

 

“Sor— Sorry?” Mimi asked, utterly bewildered. “What is there for that girl to be sorry for?!”

 

[“P-Petra!” Subaru exclaimed with a similar level of confusion, panicking at the sight of
the sobbing little girl. “What's wrong? Why are you apologizing?]

 

[“I'm sorry,” Petra apologized again, continuing to cry. “I'm sorry…! I'm so sorry…”]

 

“Why?!” Julius asked, looking even more panicked than Subaru at the sight of the crying
child. “Why are you crying?! What’s wrong?!”

 

Ferris couldn’t help snickering at his friend’s frantic helplessness. Julius never had been very
good with kids.

 

[“Father said you’d brought all of us back,” Petra sobbed. “He said you’d gotten a little
injured, and had had a hard time… But then I saw you lying there, and— How was that
only a little—?!”]

 

[It took a while for Petra to calm down enough to explain why she was apologizing.]



 

Garfiel swallowed. It hurt, to see Petra like this. She was normally so headstrong and
confident. To see her this distraught…

 

“I know,” Otto muttered, even though Garfiel hadn’t said anything out loud. “I know.”

 

Frederica could only watch with a pained look on her face. Petra had always been such a
good girl, after all. Even if she had been rather mischievous when she was young.

 

Emilia looked up with sad eyes. It was good, that Subaru had eventually recovered — but she
had always hated how badly he had scared the townsfolk with those awful injuries of his.

 

(It was nice, that they had been worried about him. But Emilia didn’t like seeing them cry.)

 

Beatrice only sighed. How bothersome people could be, she supposed.

 

[She’d brought Meili into the fold. She’d loved the puppy that turned out to be a
mabeast. She had let it run away into the forest when she should have looked after it
more carefully.]

 

“Aw…” Julius’ eyes filled with sympathy. “Oh, Petra…”

 

Ricardo smiled, a little wistful. After — everything else — he had seen so far, it felt
somewhat odd to see someone so tearful over mistakes that had been so fundamentally
childish.

 

Mimi sighed. “Children can be so naïve,” she murmured. “…Mimi’s glad that Subaru was
there to catch those children when they fell.”

 

Tivey and Hetaro both pressed close to their big sister, feeling much the same way.



 

Anastasia hummed. A little girl who already had enough of a sense of responsibility to hold
herself accountable for the harm caused by her careless actions, even well-intentioned as they
had been… Really, the more she saw of this girl, the more that Anastasia couldn’t help but be
impressed.

 

[She had led everyone into the forest, even while knowing they weren’t supposed to be
there. They had looked to her for answers just like they always did, and she had…!]

 

Crusch shivered. A little girl like that, shouldering the fates of her peers in a situation that
had quickly turned so dire…! What a cruel set of circumstances that could have turned into,
had something happened that ended up being truly irreversible.

 

Wilhelm winced. He knew what an awful feeling it was, to feel that you had made a mistake
at the cost of your men. It was a necessary lesson for all young ones to learn eventually, but
he wished Petra hadn’t needed to experience it in a situation that ended up having such high
stakes.

 

Ferris sighed. He had always known that boys were silly, but he guessed girls were often
quite silly, too.

 

[And worst of all, at the end, Petra had been the one to send Subaru into the darkness of
the forest to find the missing Meili. And that was what had ultimately led to Subaru
getting mauled so terribly that he almost lost his life.]

 

—Well, Felt winced. Perhaps that was sort of her fault. But to feel guilty about trying to help
someone you were worried about was ridiculous.

 

“He’s the one who went in after her,” Rachins muttered. “Blame him, he’s the idiot here.”

 

Was everyone in the Emilia Camp like this? Old Man Rom couldn’t help but chuckle: he was
starting to believe that faction was an entire camp full of children.



 

Reinhard frowned. Petra had asked for help, hadn’t she? Helping those who asked for it was
— it was simply the right thing to do. Why would she feel bad about that? He felt like he was
missing something important, and it ached when he realized that he didn’t know what it was.

 

[“Like I said,” Petra finished with a sniffle, tears still running down her face.
“Everything is my fault.”]

 

Crusch couldn’t help but smile tenderly. Petra had been wrestling with all this guilt, but all
Subaru had been worrying about was what he might have done to her. It seemed that
misunderstanding had made Petra angry rather than touched, but Crusch couldn’t help but
look fondly at someone with that sort of personality.

 

Not that it was a surprise, where Subaru was concerned. Certainly not after all Crusch had
seen from him so far.

 

—Frederica smiled somewhat sadly. It had been more than just Subaru’s injuries that had
shaken her to her core, she knew.

 

All her life, Petra had managed to weasel her way out of trouble due to her cuteness — or,
really, because her village adored her so. She had never really had to beg for forgiveness, or
even felt like she needed to apologize for its own sake. Seeing Subaru lying there, injured to
the point where he had nearly died, all for her sake…

 

Petra had learned a lot, thanks to that nasty awakening. The realization that it was the
kindness of her family and neighbors that kept letting her get away with things, as opposed to
simple foolishness on their parts; the weight of the consequences her actions could have — or
perhaps, already had — brought down upon those around her; the painful bite of regret that
felt far too great to ever be forgiven at all.

 

(It was honestly rather foolish: Petra had only ever been a child, and the things that she
regretted were little more than the usual reckless decisions made by a little girl too
headstrong for her own good. But all of this had meant a lot to her, so Frederica would not
dare belittle any of it.)



 

[Subaru listened patiently, all the way to the very end. And then he was quiet for a long,
long moment.]

 

In the present moment, Subaru could only quietly shake his head at that foolish, good-hearted
little girl. He knew how this memory had gone already, of course, but he couldn’t help feeling
somewhat wistful all the same.

 

Ah, Petra, he thought. You’ve always been too kind for your own good, haven’t you…?

 

[“…You know, Petra,” Subaru finally said.]

 

(Though really, Subaru felt that he could say that about a number of the people he knew.)

 

[“…Yes,” Petra whispered, gnashing her teeth in fearful anticipation for what he might
say next.]

 

She didn’t need to worry, Ram knew. She had engaged barely more mischief than what could
be expected of a young girl her age, after all. Subaru had looked past far, far worse — before
turning around to say that he loved her.

 

She didn’t need to worry, Rem knew. Because Subaru was perhaps the most forgiving sort of
person that she could imagine.

 

But, more than just looking for forgiveness, Petra believed that she was guilty. And when a
person believed themselves guilty…

 

[“Not that it's your fault, Petra…” Subaru began, sounding somewhat hesitant. “You're
wrong. If you have apologized… It's not.”]

 



Rem sighed. That wasn’t a satisfying answer, not to someone who genuinely believed that
they had wronged Subaru to such an extent. And from Petra’s expression, she could tell that
this answer had done nothing but perhaps make her feel even worse.

 

Reinhard felt hopelessly lost. Just what was someone supposed to say, in a situation like this?
What could Subaru do to comfort that crying child, if assuring her that she hadn’t done
anything wrong wasn’t enough?

 

He didn’t understand. He wished he did.

 

[“Hmm…” A look of understanding overcame Subaru’s face. “Maybe this is it.”]

 

“Hmm…?” Felt tilted her head. Nearby, Anastasia had a similar look of interest.

 

[“—I forgive you,” Subaru decided.]

 

Crusch’s tender smile broke into something much wider, a glow of pride entering her soft
eyes. What a considerate, compassionate, empathetic response…!

 

Really, between Subaru and Lady Emilia, Crusch wondered if the overflowing kindness
would be enough to melt her heart inside her chest.

 

[Petra blinked, looking somewhat shocked.]

 

[“Well, it's true that you made a lot of mistakes, Petra,” Subaru said. “I felt it would be
different if I irresponsibly just said ‘There's nothing to be sorry for.’ And so, when I
think about what the best thing to say to this tearful, remorseful Petra would be…”]

 

“Honestly,” Rom murmured, shaking his head. “What other answer could anyone have
expected, here?”



 

[Petra was still listening intently, her eyes round.]

 

It was Subaru, after all. Ricardo chuckled, shaking his head.

 

[“I forgive you, Petra,” Subaru declared with a smile. “Don't worry. I'm not angry. I'm
just glad that you and Meina don't have any scars.” He laughed. “But not me and
Lucas. A man's scars are his badge of honor!”]

 

“Hell yeah!” Garfiel crowed, pumping his fist into the air.

 

Otto sighed at them both, personally not being quite so sure. Though, if he said that out loud,
no doubt they’d both start poking fun at his manhood again. Troublesome personalities, both
of those two…

 

[Petra made a croaking noise, her face wide filled a very specific sort of wonder at the
sight of Subaru’s laughing face.]

 

“—I forgive you, too, you know,” Subaru suddenly said.

 

Rem and Ram startled at being addressed, looking over to see him staring at them both with a
hopeful expression on his face.

 

“I…forgave you both a long time ago,” he said. His voice was unusually meek and hesitant.
“Really, I did. Maybe you made some mistakes, but…you know?”

 

It was a ridiculous comparison, Rem thought, to place herself and this little girl side by side.
What Rem had done wasn’t the same as a naïve little girl carelessly following a puppy into
the forest with her friends, and then asking the grown-up who came to save them to go after
the one child still missing from the lot. Rem had—

 



“If you don’t resist, I can grant you a quick end.”

 

Rem had—

 

“I will not be able to ask you anything if I let you die so easily.”

 

She had—

 

“Mana of water, heal this body.”

 

She—

 

“My sister is too kind.”

 

—Subaru said he forgave her. He probably meant it, even. But could Rem really accept that
and be done with it all?

 

But for some reason, Rem found herself unable to muster the heart to snap at that face of his
this time. This wasn’t like when he had been arguing, and yelling, and fighting tooth and nail
to defend the indefensible. The way he was looking at her, with the big hopeful eyes of a boy
who had only ever wanted to be her friend…

 

Just what was she supposed to do in a situation like this? Was there even a right answer, here?

 

“…Can you just give us a bit of time, Subaru?” Her older sister finally answered. Her voice
was quiet. “It’s— I didn’t even know I had DONE something like that. I just…need some
time, alright?”

 

Subaru bit his lip, but then finally acquiesced with a nod of his head.



 

[“Oh, Petra.” Subaru greeted the young girl with a smile the very next day. “You're all
dressed up today.”]

 

“Ah.” Anastasia smiled, amused. “She dressed up for him, did she…?”

 

Crusch dimly wondered if her younger self had ever dressed up for a boy she liked, but
dismissed the thought as irrelevant after a moment. The scene in front of her was too sweet
for her to get melancholic over it.

 

[“Heh, heh,” Petra giggled, picking up the hem of her skirt and twirling around.
“Right? Isn't it cute? Isn't it cute?”]

 

Ricardo chuckled. It looked as though someone was developing a bit of a crush. Petra didn’t
need to worry: that sort of puppy love was always adorable to watch.

 

[“Oh, you look super cute,” Subaru agreed warmly. “Where did you get that outfit?”]

 

[Petra hesitated.]

 

“She didn’t steal it, did she?” Julius muttered tiredly. He didn’t want to make assumptions,
but considering everything else this Camp had apparently been up to...

 

“Give her the benefit of the doubt, would you?” Crusch scolded lightly, even as she held back
a laugh at his exhausted reaction. Wilhelm just chuckled, shaking his head.

 

[“Umm, you know. This is…” Petra shook her head. “I didn't actually buy it! I made
it!”]

 

Anastasia blinked. “Oh?”



 

[“You made it?” Subaru repeated, eyes widening with surprise before turning into a
mixture of understanding and satisfaction. “Oh, I see! Oh, right, right, right. Petra,
that's awesome!”]

 

[Petra puffed out her chest at the praise, her cheeks pink.]

 

Otto resisted a groan, thinking of Subaru’s own hobby.

 

[“Petra, as expected, you have good taste,” Subaru declared. “I'm sure you could open a
store in the future.”]

 

He wondered if Subaru had ever considered opening a clothing store himself. It annoyed and
worried him, that he could picture it so clearly.

 

—Garfiel suddenly shook him by the shoulder, snapping him out of it. “Look at Petra’s face!”
he whispered with a snicker.

 

[“…Really?” Petra was saying. Her voice was oddly meek. “You think so?”]

 

[“Hm?” Subaru tilted his head, looking somewhat confused at her lack of cheer.]

 

Otto blinked, startled by that reaction himself. He knew well and good about Petra’s crush, of
course — but to see the girl who annoyingly insisted on teasing him day in and day out acting
so shy was very strange. Her familiar call of “Ottotototo-saaan~!” echoed through his head
as he stared at the meteor.

 

Barf, Felt thought, just barely resisting the urge to roll her eyes.

 

…Petra probably could, actually.



 

The more that Anastasia watched this young girl, the more interested she became in her
potential. With taste like that, and a hardworking nature that led her to start practicing
already, Petra could likely go far as a seamstress. The only thing missing was…

 

[“You know,“ Petra suddenly said. She sounded nervous. “In the future, I want to go to
the Royal Capital to work as a tailor. —Th-This dress is practice for that… It's only one
dress, but I-I'll practice more, and then…”]

 

And there it was: the ambition. Anastasia smiled proudly. She would have to keep an eye out
for a young, orange-haired Capital seamstress in the coming years, it seemed.

 

Felt could respect someone who had a lofty dream that they intended to make their own
someday through hard work. That was the sort of integrity she admired in others, and that she
would always fight to cultivate within herself.

 

Even if that voice and those eyes made her want to gag right now.

 

Frederica remembered. Petra had told her once, she thought, or perhaps she had figured it out
on her own. Many of the others in her village hadn’t taken that dream of hers seriously,
dismissing it as the fantasies of a little girl. She hadn’t really cared what any of them thought
about it, but then Subaru had come along, and Petra had been worried.

 

[“That's a nice dream,” Subaru smiled. “I bet you will become the best tailor in the
Royal Capital.”]

 

But then, of course, Subaru had responded to her dream in exactly the right way.

 

Beatrice smiled. It was a nice dream, she supposed. And it was just like her contractor to
respond to a dream like that in such a manner — and by the look of it, to mean every word he
said.

 



Emilia giggled. It was a nice dream, and she was sure that Petra would achieve it one day.
Petra was a very talented girl, after all.

 

[“—Ah.”]

 

[And Petra looked back at Subaru with big round eyes, her cheeks turning a wonderful
shade of red.]

 

And that was how that happened, wasn’t it? Garfiel couldn’t help but snicker a little at the
look on Petra’s face.

 

—Well. He guessed there were worse reasons to fall in love with someone.

 

“…So,” Ram said, watching the mundane exchange play out onscreen. She sounded
exhausted. “Is that it? Are we done, now?”

 

She already had a feeling the answer was no.

 

“I wanna be done,” Rachins muttered. “Please say we’re done…”

 

“Most likely not, I’m afraid,” Anastasia said. Her tone grew somewhat clipped. “The meteor
is still going.”

 

“What more is there to see?” Wilhelm asked weakly. “Surely there isn’t…”

 

He didn’t want to think about what it might mean if…

 

Rom silently steeled himself for what was to come. Considering all he’d heard about that boy
getting up to over the past year, he had somewhat expected that they weren’t at the end of it



yet.

 

Ricardo exhaled slowly. “Well,” he announced, clapping his hands. His tone was forcefully
cheerful. “Nothing to do but wait and see, eh?”

 

Ferris groaned loudly. It could have been a sob. Crusch winced, rubbing his shoulders. For
his sake, she hoped this wouldn’t go on for too much longer.

 

“…Mimi would rather see it than not,” Mimi declared after a moment. Her eyes were fierce.
“Even if it’s unpleasant, Mimi can’t just turn away from it. Not when it’s this important.”

 

Her two brothers nodded their heads in agreement, both due to similar feelings in each of
their hearts and because they would both follow their big sister’s lead no matter what.

 

“Hopefully it’ll get a bit easier to watch from here,” Julius said, trying to keep his voice level.
“It’s… I just hope we’ve gotten through the worst of it.”

 

“If we have, then good for us,” Felt said. “If we haven’t, I’m with Mimi: I’d rather see it than
not. This is too important for me to to turn away from.”

 

Reinhard bowed his head, grateful for his Lady’s consideration for the boy he considered his
very best friend.

 

“Really wish I had a say in all this,” Subaru muttered uncomfortably. “They’re MY
memories, you know…”

 

“Don’t worry, Captain!” Garfiel declared, trying to put on a brave face. If this continued until
Sanctuary— “All this has done is made ya look even cooler in my eyes, honest!”

 

“We’ll stand by you no matter what, Natsuki-san,” Otto said, voice gentle. “I know it’s
unpleasant, but once we know what you can’t tell us outright we’ll be able to help you with



everything we’ve got. So…try to bear with it?”

 

“Not like I have much of a choice, here,” Subaru sighed.

 

Frederica winced. Subaru was right, of course, about the invasiveness of this situation: she
couldn’t imagine the discomfort of being in his position right now. But it seemed that
everyone understood the situation enough to be kind about it, doing their best to keep their
reactions to Subaru’s past behavior light and playful. That consideration was a blessing, at
least.

 

“We’ll need to have a chat once this is over, of course,” Emilia murmured. Her heart still
ached painfully in her chest.

 

Subaru winced. “Emilia—”

 

“But that can wait,” Emilia declared, voice firm. “That’s not something we should be getting
into right now. For now…”

 

“For now, Betty’s contractor should try to relax, in fact,” Beatrice agreed. She pressed her
hand against the glass. “Betty is here, so there’s no need to worry, in fact.”

 

Subaru’s face broke into a smile. “That’s true,” he murmured. “So long as my Beako is here
with me, I can handle anything!”

 

Rem winced. Anything?

 

Next to her, Ram sighed. “We really will have a lot to talk about,” she muttered. “But we’ll
be able to talk about it, at least. That’s better than where we were before.”

 

…Right. Rem had only just opened her eyes in this very theater, but — it sounded like a full
year had passed between then and now, right? A full year in which nobody had known what



was happening right under their noses, and in which neither she nor her sister had
understood…

 

Well. They both knew what had happened, now. So now that the wound that had been left to
fester in darkness had at last been uncovered, they could dress it properly so that it could
finally heal well.

 

Rem wasn’t sure if Subaru was telling lying about being mostly over it, or if he believed he
was telling the truth about it, or if he seriously didn’t think about it much anymore. But now
that she and her sister knew, they could figure out where Subaru was and meet him where he
had already come to meet them halfway, hand as outstretched as it always was. That—

 

As uncomfortable as it might be, Rem believed that honest effort would be a good place to
start, when it came to building a new and shiny relationship with this boy she knew loved her
with all his heart and soul.

 

With that, Rem turned back to the meteor, ready to face the future as the clock ticked on, and
on, and on…
