SIDE STORIES INCLUDED:

[The World Petra Saw]



Chapter 19: Eccentric Tastes (SS 1, Part 1)
Chapter Summary

Subaru recovers from his first week at the manor. The other residents do some nice
things for him.

Chapter Notes
See the end of the chapter for notes

[“Nee-sama, Nee-sama!” Rem said excitedly. “Please listen to this. Today, Subaru-kun
was able to get out of bed.”]

 

[“Hmm, yes.”]

 

Julius winced. With how injured Subaru had been after his second encounter with the
Wolgarm, it was perhaps indeed a thing to celebrate that he was not completely bedridden.
Though the boy had been able to go to the village the very next day, there was a definite
difference between mustering up the energy to check on the people you had just risked your
life to save from certain death and being able to return to the tedious work of usual, daily life.

 

Anastasia exhaled slowly, a grim look on her face as she thought much the same thing as her
knight. Though, on top of that…

 

“That sure is some change, ain’t it?” Tivey muttered. The night-and-day difference with how
Rem was behaving around Subaru now sent a chill down his spine.

 

“I prefer it,” Hetaro said quietly. “I’m glad that Rem likes him now.”

 

Mimi didn’t know what words could properly describe her revulsion at this turn of events, so
she settled for curling her lip and hugging both of her little brothers tight.

 



“So we’re watching Rem’s memories alongside Subaru’s, now, eh…?” Rom frowned for a
moment, and then shrugged. It was probably their captor’s way of being considerate, sparing
no expense in fulfilling the girl’s heartfelt request.

 

[“Nee-sama, Nee-sama. I’ve promised to cut Subaru-kun’s hair. What kind of haircut
do you think would look good on him? He looks wonderful no matter what, but…”]

 

[“Ah, hmm, yes.”]

 

Reinhard reflected on the joy he felt at adorning his Lady with different beautiful dresses. He
smiled. Perhaps he understood what Rem’s feelings were, when it came to this special thing.

 

(Across the room, Felt scowled. She could just tell that her dumbass knight was thinking
something sappy.)

 

Frederica giggled at the growing bewilderment on Ram’s face. Ram wasn’t in reach to smack
her for the mirth dancing in her eyes, so she kept giggling and giggling and giggling, and just
couldn’t seem to stop.

 

She may not have been in a laughing mood, but Emilia smiled weakly nearby. “That’s nice,”
she murmured. “I’m glad you managed to keep that promise, Subaru… I’m so glad that the
two of you managed that much.”

 

After all, the inherent importance of a promise aside… Emilia knew that this particular vow
had meant so very much to him, and for so very long.

 

Wilhelm cringed at the thought of Subaru actually going through with that promise. He knew
that it had been important to the boy, of course, but still…!

 

Rom crossed his arms, and tried not to let his unease show. It wasn’t really fair for him to feel
uneasy about that proposal, after all, for a number of reasons.



 

Otto thought about Subaru willingly allowing this woman to approach his neck and head with
a sharp object and buried his face in his hands.

 

[“Nee-sama, Nee-sama. Just now, Subaru-kun was able to go to the bathroom by
himself. Please compliment him!”]

 

Rem choked. “E-Eh?!”

 

Next to her, Rachins barked out a laugh. He wasn’t the only one.

 

[“Hmm…?”]

 

Ram exhaled slowly, trying to hide her disbelief as she searched for words that would be
appropriate for this situation. “…My younger sister sure is full of surprises,” she finally
managed to say.

 

Rem — couldn’t really argue with that.

 

Across the room, Garfiel had devolved into loud cackles. “Oh, Captain!” he crowed, tears of
mirth in his eyes. Subaru was squawking back at him, face scarlet. “The indignity, to be told
that— Oh, my amazin’ self is so sorry—!”

 

Nearby, Otto was trying and failing to stifle giggles of his own. For Rem to declare that using
the bathroom, of all things, warranted praise…! Oh, his poor manly pride. —Though
considering some of the jokes Subaru made at Otto’s expense, perhaps this was deserved.

 

“It’s nyot that much of a stretch, actually,” Ferris said. Those who turned to him were
surprised to not see a hint of teasing on his face. “With injuries as severe as that… Subaru-
kyun being able to use the bathroom on his own so soon afterwards isn’t something to take
for granted.”



 

And just like that, all of Garfiel’s amusement drained away — as did that of everyone else in
the theater, leaving the room utterly silent.

 

Crusch grimaced. That was right. Subaru’s injuries… He was doing a good job of hiding it,
but they had been incredibly vicious, and were clearly still bothering him now no matter how
badly the figure before them wanted to pretend that they weren’t. It wasn’t actually a
laughing matter, not at all.

 

The idea that he may have struggled to so much as use the bathroom on his own afterwards,
as the price for his bravery… Somehow, that sobering, mortifying image struck Crusch’s
heart in a manner that no other detail about his injuries from that final fight against the
Wolgarm had quite managed.

 

Julius shifted. Come to think of it… Hadn’t Subaru still sported these injuries, the day of the
Royal Selection Ceremony? It was hard for him to remember every detail from that day,
especially when so many more important things had happened at around that same time, but
—

 

—Felt huffed loudly, drawing attention to herself as she made a show of leaning her cheek
against her hand. “Still,” she said, in a tone forcefully made lighthearted. “Demanding that
your big sis COMPLIMENT the poor guy over it… Sheesh.” She flashed Rem a teasing grin.
“Are your standards really that low?”

 

“Ho— How embarrassing,” Rachins added, quickly catching on to Felt’s intent. Somewhere
beneath her teasing grin, Felt smiled slightly: he did have his moments. “What a blow to his
pride as a man! Have you no mercy?!”

 

Rem managed to smile weakly back at the two of them.

 

Beatrice didn’t smile at all. Her expression had remained serious all the way through.

 



Subaru shifted, looking worried and uncomfortable. “I’d prefer it if my Beako would laugh a
little…” he prodded.

 

Beatrice cut her eyes away from him, feeling somewhere between indignant at his outrageous
request and ashamed at herself not being able to fulfill it. “…Betty is sorry, Subaru.”

 

[“Roswaal-sama, Roswaal-sama…!”]

 

[“Hmmmm~?”]

 

[Rem was beaming. And then, behind Subaru’s back—]

 

Ram choked.

 

“Wait—” Subaru’s eyes went wide. “Wait, Rem — you spent your entire saved-up salary on
my replacement butler uniform?!”

 

Rem stared at the meteor. “I— guess??” she offered, even more clueless than Subaru about
this development.

 

[From the look on her sister’s face later that day, as Subaru was getting all dressed up,
Ram’s old self seemed particularly dissatisfied with the fact that Subaru had not even
been made aware of this detail.]

 

“He really should have paid for it himself,” Julius commented, crossing his arms with a
frown on his face.

 

Mimi’s eyes widened. “Eh?!” she demanded.

 



“What?” Julius blinked, looking rather surprised by her loud, shocked objection. “Subaru was
injured while defending HIS household, protecting HIS village, saving HIS servant — with
all due respect, the absolute least that Lord Roswaal should have done after all of that was
replace HIS household’s uniform that had ended up tattered in the process. How is that even a
question?”

 

“Oh.” Mimi relaxed. “Oh, Mimi thought— Yeah, that makes more sense.”

 

“Not to mention Natsuki-kun belongs to the Margrave,” Anastasia added, her expression
dark. “That’s what it means to accept a request from someone to be yer servant: it means they
belong to you, and that you’ll take care of them accordingly. Lord Roswaal normally seems
to understand this, so…”

 

Suddenly her expression cleared.

 

Tivey frowned. “Lady Anastasia?”

 

“Ah,” the Merchant Princess grinned. “Ah, I get it.”

 

“Eh?” Hetaro tilted his head. “Get what?”

 

Anastasia giggled. “He coulda paid for the uniform just fine,” she said teasingly. “Probably
would have, in normal circumstances. …But it seems someone else really, REALLY wanted
to do it.”

 

Catching on, Ricardo barked out a laugh. “Oh, little lady!” he cackled. “Ya just couldn’t help
yerself, could ya?!”

 

Having been sneakily listening to their conversation nearby, Rem’s face turned bright red at
being suddenly addressed. “Ah—”

 



Ram was no help at all, giggling to herself and doing nothing else she watched her little sister
flounder at all the amused gazes being turned her way.

 

[“Did I keep you waiting?”]

 

A certain voice suddenly spoke aloud. It wasn’t a particularly loud voice, but it cut through
the din of the theater regardless, quelling everyone with an effortless wave of its hand.

 

[“No,” Subaru assured the owner of that voice, himself having been waiting patiently
before the tree the two of them had decided to meet at. “I’ve only just gotten here
myself.”]

 

After all, while Rem was stuck dealing with her newfound obsession, Subaru had headed out
to finally make good on a promise several lifetimes in the making.

 

—Crusch blinked. “Wait,” she said, frowning. “That can’t be right. All those pictures of the
Great Spirit around the tree… You must have arrived much earlier than Lady Emilia, if you
drew all of them in the dirt to kill time before she came!”

 

[“You said you wanted to meet outside the mansion, and say that stuff we just said…”
Emilia tilted her head, glancing back up in the direction from which she had come.
“Can I ask if there was any particular meaning to that?”]

 

[“They both seem rather fitting for a date, don’t you think?” Subaru said cheerfully.
“Leaving the mansion together wouldn’t feel very much like a date, and when you meet
outside the sort of conversation we just had is an absolute necessity!”]

 

“Wait—” Subaru’s eyes widened. “Wait, we’re watching THIS?!”

 

[“Hmm, so that’s how it is. I really don’t know anything about this sort of thing.”]

 



“Oh!” Felt cackled. “Oh, THAT’s what’s going on, is it?!”

 

[“By the way, I would still reply ‘I’ve only just gotten here myself’ even if you were
super late, it’s a sign of my noble manly heart.”]

 

Anastasia coughed lightly, having figured it out herself. “That sentiment doesn’t really work
if ya say it out loud like that,” she offered.

 

[“But wouldn’t that mean you were reeeeally late too…”]

 

[“There’s certain things you shouldn’t point out even if you notice, aren’t there?!”]

 

Subaru sputtered, eyes darting around for a long moment as he tried to figure out a rebuttal to
Anastasia, to Emilia, to all those amused gazes peering his way — before he finally gave up
and buried his scarlet face in his hands.

 

(Rem sighed quietly in relief as Subaru’s misfortune turned everyone’s attention across the
room, away from her own reddened cheeks.)

 

(Well, almost everyone: Ram’s warm, mirthful gaze was still fixed firmly upon her little
sister.)

 

[“Eh, what’s wrong?” Emilia frowned. “Do I look weird somehow?”]

 

Anastasia started laughing at the look on Subaru’s face. “Boys…!”

 

“They really are wolves, hmm?” Ferris grinned.

 



[“The characters for weird and romance look quite similar, huh, but setting that
aside…” Subaru’s hand was on his jaw, his eyes staring intently at Emilia’s appearance.
“There’s only a tiny bit that’s weird about you, and that tiny bit is also charming in
itself so it’s all good. More importantly, you’re looking extraordinarily cute today as
well! …Have you dressed up a little more than usual today?”]

 

[“You noticed?” Emilia said, surprised.]

 

“Of course he’d notice,” Felt cackled. “He could be oblivious to everything else in the world,
but never to his precious Emilia-tan, eh?”

 

“Someday you’ll end up just as head-over-heels for someone as Subaru is for her,” Rom
teased.

 

“Od Laguna no!” Felt recoiled. “If that ever happens you’d better knock some sense into me,
geez!”

 

[“Puck was a lot more enthusiastic than usual today…”]

 

[“Ooh, great job!” Subaru replied, sounding delighted. “Not bad, Puck. And here I
thought for sure that his feelings as a father would make him put up some resistance
when it came to his daughter’s first date.”]

 

[“Yeah, he was reeeeally conflicted about it,” Emilia confirmed with a faint smile. “But
he’s sleeping in my crystal right now so you can relax.”]

 

Beatrice smiled weakly. She could only imagine Bubby’s conflicted feelings on the matter.

 

Still, she was happy that he had managed to put them aside for the sake of her contractor and
his silly elf girl being able to spend that day together.

 



[“I see.” A relieved expression flickered across Subaru’s face for a moment, and then he
cleared his throat and humbly bowed before the beautiful woman.]

 

Donned in his new, flawless-looking butler outfit — the only formal clothing he possessed —
Subaru for once looked as though his formal behavior matched his appearance. Julius found
himself smiling.

 

[“Well then,” Subaru declared, extending out his elbow as if to link arms with Emilia. “I
suppose this is the beginning of our first date. I consider it a great honor that you would
allow me to escort you.”]

 

Julius’ smile graduated into a fit of giggles.

 

Subaru squawked, face growing scarlet. “What’re YOU laughing at?!”

 

He didn’t mean to laugh. Truly, he didn’t. But—

 

But Subaru just looked so adorably HAPPY then and there, didn’t he?

 

[“Umm…” Emilia’s fingers hesitantly grasped his cuff, as opposed to his hand. “Is this
alright?”]

 

Wilhelm’s eyes widened, and he coughed into his fist. “Oh dear,” he croaked.

 

An adorable and gentle demeanor like that… Wilhelm thought it would me any man’s
greatest weakness, if a girl were to grasp at the cusp of their sleeve with a look like that on
her face.

 

Anastasia giggled. If she didn’t know any better, she’d think that Emilia had done that to poor
Subaru on purpose. Either way, she had to admit that it had been expertly done.



 

Emilia remembered this. Puck had told her beforehand not to take Subaru’s hand, so she had
been unsure about what to do instead. She had been anxious that Subaru would be
disappointed or angry with her in response, but instead—

 

[“This isn’t what I was hoping for, but that’s a performance beyond my expectations!”
Subaru exclaimed, covering his face with his palms as he squirmed about with a rosy
face. “Your loveliness truly is fanatical like an Oni…!”]

 

Wilhelm chuckled, his heart unusually giddy at the sight he understood so very well. Subaru,
blushing bright, found himself unable to say a word in response.

 

Emilia winced. That phrase again, was it? She really didn’t…

 

But it was a compliment, as far as Subaru was concerned. And because he had considered it a
compliment, she had no choice but to smile warmly back at him.

 

[“So,” Emilia was saying, pulling on Subaru’s cuff as they walked side by side. “What
exactly do you do on a ‘date’?”]

 

[“First of all, we’ll head to the village,” Subaru answered. “After that, we’ll pay our
respects to the dead…”]

 

“Eh?” Garfiel frowned. “But…”

 

But nobody had died.

 

“What?” Ricardo asked. “Why would ya do that? Isn’t that a little dismal, for an outing with
a girl ya like?”

 



“I didn’t mind one bit,” Emilia said forcefully. “I was happy to share that moment with
Subaru, of course I was!”

 

This response  made almost everyone in the room appear even more confused than before.
Having already figured it out, however, Crusch felt her eyes go soft.

 

…Or at least, Garfiel corrected himself, still lost on his own thoughts, nobody had STAYED
dead. And Captain didn’t seem like the type to host his own funeral, did he?

 

…Should he be granted a proper funeral, actually? He was still alive, but he had gone
through death. Would it be helpful, if they were to give his old selves their proper rites? Or
would it cause more harm than good?

 

Garfiel didn’t know. He hadn’t heard of any folktales where the hero had died and come back
to life, so he didn’t really know what he was supposed to do.

 

[“And then, how about going to see some flowers?” Subaru declared. “Slowly, calmly,
there’s no rush.”]

 

[“That sounds nice,” Emilia replied, and she meant every word.]

 

Frederica chuckled. “That sounds much more proper for an outing with a girl, Subaru-
sama…”

 

Garfiel remembered taking Ram to see the snow white sakuras, of course, and now he knew
that he had taken Rem as well. The memory made him relax a bit. Flower-viewing was
something he had experience with, at least.

 

[The children had prepared a bouquet for Subaru in advance, like he had requested.
But, of course, they didn’t allow him to leave his encounter with them unscathed.
Important date or not, these innocent children did not care even a little bit.]



 

Subaru scoffed, folding his arms and turning away with a huff and a bright pink blush on his
cheeks as the rest of the theater laughed at his predicament. Darn brats.

 

[“Thank goodness the children seem alright,” Emilia smiled. “You seemed reeeeeally
popular too, Subaru.”]

 

[“I wonder if that’s something to be so happy about,” Subaru muttered, dusting off his
butler outfit. “It’s actually pretty problematic in its own way, Emilia-tan.”]

 

“Suure it is,” Ferris laughed. Julius simply shook his head, a smile on his face. There were
some things that Subaru would never admit, perhaps, but that didn’t make it any less obvious
to anyone giving him even half of their attention.

 

[“Even with this, they were probably holding back because you were there. If it weren’t
for that, I’d be going through something even more horrible right about now.”]

 

[“Come on, you’re exaggerating. Those kids just like you, isn’t that right.”]

 

“So overdramatic,” Old Man Rom teased.

 

Wilhelm huffed. “Kids are annoying,” he agreed somberly. “But as the future of our great
country, they must be trained regardless. …Kid-friendly types like Subaru-dono are ideal for
that, it seems.”

 

“What kind of backhanded compliment is that?!”

 

[“If this were any other day, I would have snot spread all over my back right now.
Fortunately, I was able to avoid that fate today.”]

 



[“That’s what usually happens?!” Emilia exclaimed, her eyes filling with pity. Subaru’s
expression turned somewhat complicated, and he ended up averting his gaze.]

 

Crusch shook her head. He just couldn’t be honest, could he? Always playing up this weird
act in front of the people he cared about — what was even the point of that? And then, even
on the rare occasions they took him seriously, he found himself backing away from it…

 

What was the point of all this? She just didn’t understand it at all.

 

Ricardo grimaced. If he were being honest, he wasn’t all that fond of brats himself. It was
because of that, perhaps, that he couldn’t help but watch the Subaru onscreen with a sort of
admiration: it was always easier to admire people with skills that you couldn’t imagine
developing yourself.

 

“I think yer selling yerself short, Ricardo,” Anastasia commented wryly, guessing his
thoughts from the look on his face.

 

He denied it, of course. “Dunno what yer talking about, Ana-bo.”

 

Men. Anastasia rolled her eyes. They never could just be honest about themselves, could
they?

 

[“Ah,” Subaru suddenly said. Emilia turned around as well.]

 

Ricardo busted out in loud laughter, quickly followed by the rest of the theater, at the sight of
the gaggle of children having followed the two of them — followed SUBARU — close
behind.

 

“You see what I mean?!” Subaru demanded. “Darn brats, you take your eyes off of them for
even a second—!”

 



“Betty’s contractor sure is popular, in fact,” Beatrice giggled. “And he’s very bad at
pretending he doesn’t like it, I suppose…”

 

Subaru threw up his hands. “Betrayed by my own Beako?!”

 

And yet again, this injustice he faced was the fault of none other than the brats.

 

[“Come on, you guys can’t tag along this time,” Subaru was scolding, making a shooing
motion with his hand. “I told you that Emilia and I were going to be having a thrilling,
lascivious tryst, didn’t I? Get outta here, scram!”]

 

[“Ehh, what a tyrant.” “Ehh, what a rude guy.” “Ehh, what an unruly kid.”]

 

[“I’m no unruly brat.”]

 

Julius snorted loudly before he could stop himself.

 

“Ju— Julius!” Anastasia scolded, trying desperately (and failing) to stifle her laughter.
Across the room, Subaru’s outraged squawking sound caused the roar of laughter within the
theater to nearly triple in volume.

 

[“Also, we’re getting close to the barrier,” Subaru reminded them. “Which if you
remember you were forbidden from approaching. Unless you want to hear Muraosa’s
long, boring, droning lectures, you’d better head back right now. Head back, and have
fun playing that frozen Oni game I taught you or something.”]

 

Anastasia had watched him teach the children that game, alongside everyone else. “Freeze
Tag,” according to his hometown, but renamed “for more universal appeal.” It was a cute sort
of children’s game, really.

 



[Most of the children went away without an issue, grumbling quietly about Subaru
having chased them off — but Petra stayed behind for a moment, staring at Emilia with
a look that made the silver-haired girl’s charmed smile falter slightly.]

 

“Ah,” Felt snickered.

 

“Oh dear,” Anastasia laughed.

 

“Oh,” Garfiel grinned. “Seems someone’s found a rival, eh?”

 

[Petra’s eyes finally met Emilia’s — at which point she rudely stuck her tongue out with
a noise before running after her friends.]

 

Frederica squawked. “Petra?!”

 

Anastasia sighed, shaking her head in momentary disappointment and disapproval. Such
potential, but then there was still that childishness… She’d be sure to train it out of her, if
given the chance.

 

Felt just threw back her head and laughed.

 

[“That Petra, what’s with that attitude of hers?” Subaru sighed. “I’ll be sure to give her
a good talking to tomorrow… Are you alright, Emilia-tan? —If the shock has rendered
you unable to walk, I’m more than willing to princess carry you in my arms.”]

 

Anastasia rolled her eyes. “Ya know, that almost sounded sarcastic,” she chided. Next to her,
Mimi giggled.

 

[“…No, I’m used to it, so it’s fine.” Emilia shook her head, looking somewhat sad.
“Something of that level isn’t anything worth making a fuss over.”]



 

Ricardo’s laugh seemed to freeze. “—Ah?”

 

In fact, the entire theater had screeched to a halt.

 

“Eh…” Subaru’s amusement had been replaced by something far more serious. “Emilia…”

 

Ram’s smile faded. “So, that’s what she had thought,” she murmured.

 

Rem blinked, a little confused. “Onee-chan?” she whispered.

 

“…Lady Emilia thought that Petra was being cruel because of her looks,” Ram said quietly.
“A foolish assumption, but one that was ultimately that girl’s own fault. She could have put a
little more thought into how that reaction looked.”

 

She didn’t know why Emilia would think such a foolish thing, really. But Rem recalled how
her old self had flinched at the sight of Frederica’s teeth, back when she was a child. The
shame that blossomed inside of her at the memory made her sympathize with the little girl
who hadn’t realized what she was doing.

 

Frederica crossed her arms, disapproval growing by the minute. Even if she hadn’t meant it,
for Petra to make Lady Emilia feel like this was beyond improper.

 

[“Making a fuss, not something you hear very often these days…” Subaru pouted. “And
I’m the one hurt by the statement that you’re used to this…”]

 

Old Man Rom grimaced. Julius cringed. What a callous thing for him to say, when Emilia
had assumed Petra was…!

 

It hadn’t been Subaru’s fault. Somehow that made it feel worse.



 

“I’m oh-kay, Subaru,” Emilia said. Subaru was relieved to see that she was smiling a genuine,
happy smile. “Really, that Petra is so silly, isn’t she…?”

 

Though honestly, Emilia thought with exasperation. Petra certainly wasn’t the only silly girl
around here.

 

[“It’s fine.” Her onscreen self started walking again. “Come on, our ‘date’ isn’t over
just yet. Let’s go.”]

 

Subaru hadn’t pushed her any further about why she was sad. Emilia remembered feeling
somewhat disgusted at herself for relying on his consideration like that, but now she could
only giggle at her own foolish silliness.

 

It was nice, to have been so very wrong in her assumptions.

 

[“—Alright, we’re here, we’re here.” Subaru drew to a stop, pointing at a cluster of
trees with blue crystals marking the barrier. “We can’t enter, so sorry, but this is as far
as we go.”]

 

“Eh??” Rachins stiffened, mirth fading from his face as his eyes grew sharp. “The hell are
you doing back there?!” he demanded, visibly agitated. “The woods— Do you have a death
wish?!”

 

Ram flinched violently nearby, and then she turned to swat at him. Rachins squawked.

 

“Be more careful with your words!” she snapped.

 

—Rachins went pale once he realized what she was referring to, and then sank backwards
into a mortified silence.

 



Crusch paid neither of them any mind at all, a soft smile on her face. “I’m glad you did that
for him,” she murmured. This sort of consideration…

 

It truly was the mark of a wonderful Lady, and perhaps even of a wonderful King. Of that,
Crusch was certain.

 

Ferris’ brows were knit together. “What ARE nyew doing…?” he muttered. He hoped it
wasn’t something stupid.

 

Felt frowned for a moment, but then her gaze cleared. “Ah,” she murmured. “…Well. If that’s
what you’ve gotta do, Big Bro.”

 

Next to her, Old Man Rom sighed. It was ridiculous, but he guessed he couldn’t begrudge
this kid that little bit of comfort. If that’s what he really wanted, then…sure. He guessed that
it was fine.

 

[Before them all, Subaru took a moment to search the ground before placing the
bouquet in a secluded spot — somewhere the hands of curious children would be
unlikely to disturb it.]

 

“—Oh,” Ricardo muttered, finally catching on. “I get it.”

 

The idea of that kid genuinely mourning a Mabeast — let alone one that had hurt him so
badly, over and over again — was surreal and ridiculous, but it was also so worrying that the
mercenary captain just couldn’t bring himself to laugh. If Subaru kept on extending a hand
like that to everything in sight, even things that couldn’t even bother to recognize the
gesture…

 

But could Subaru really even stop himself? With a personality like that, would asking him to
stop be akin to ordering him to cut off his arm? As he tried to figure out how he was
supposed to feel about all this, Ricardo only knew that he felt completely out of his depth.

 



“…It’s for Subaru’s sake,” Tivey muttered. Ricardo started slightly. “This gravesite and that
bouquet were all for Subaru’s sake. So…I think it’s alright.”

 

Ricardo exhaled slowly. He understood what the kid was saying loud and clear: mourning a
Mabeast might be a ludicrous thought, but it had been important to Subaru regardless.

 

He ruffled Tivey’s hair. “Yer pretty smart, ya know that?”

 

Tivey huffed, puffing out his chest. “Of course I am,” he declared proudly. Ricardo chuckled.

 

Frederica just watched quietly, a solemn look on her face.

 

[Subaru knelt down fully and brought his hands together in prayer, closing his eyes.]

 

“Ah—” Garfiel finally caught on. His face twisted uncomfortably at the realization. “A…
Ah…”

 

Otto grimaced. He couldn’t say that he was surprised, really. It was just like Natsuki-san, to
be so foolish as to mourn a…

 

But that’s why Otto was here, after all. To make sure Subaru and Emilia could both walk in
the light, he would be the one to walk in darkness.

 

Out of respect, Beatrice quietly averted her gaze from the meteor. Her contractor would do
whatever he had to do, she supposed.

[“—MAYONNAISE!!” Subaru howled to the heavens. “I NEED IT!!”]

 

Garfiel’s concern abruptly faded away, and he threw back his head in loud laughter.

 

Otto stared at the meteor, now reflecting the bewildered eyes of the onlookers alongside
Subaru’s ambushed expression, with a look of utter disbelief dawning across his face. “…
THAT’s what this is about?!” he demanded.

 

[Natsuki Subaru is a genuine [Mayo Lover], a venerable title granted only to those who
love mayonnaise above all else, Subaru reflected solemnly. An army of culinary heretics,
topping every food imaginable with mayonnaise — commonly referred to as “mayo-ing,”
came to the world alongside the title of “Mayo Lover,” — is our justice…!]

 

“—What is ‘mayonnaise,’ exactly?” Crusch frowned.

 

Felt tilted her head. “It sounds like…a kind of food?”

 

Anastasia just giggled, piecing “mayonnaise”’s meaning together easily. A type of culinary
ingredient, widely adored as something to put over a variety of foods…yes, it wasn’t hard to
piece together what it was this boy had been thinking about.

 

To see Subaru so childishly whimpering over missing a kind of condiment he liked…!

 

[My history with mayonnaise dates back as far as the lactation period. Alongside myself,
the entire Natsuki household is utterly enthralled by mayonnaise.]

 



“Oh.” And just like that, all the amusement drained out of Anastasia’s face. “I get it,” she
murmured.

 

Mimi frowned at the oddly somber look on her Lady’s face, which seemed very much out of
place beside Subaru’s ridiculous behavior. “Boss Lady?” she asked.

 

[To have a meal without bottles of it set aside is simply unimaginable. —Cramming the
refrigerator with reserve mayonnaise was a given. Each member also marks their name on
their own personal bottles. Slurping mayonnaise straight from the bottle after a bath, the
so-called [Mayo-chuchu], had been a daily occurrence as well.]

 

Ricardo frowned. “So, it’s like…a cold drink?” he asked.

 

Having been made intimately aware of mayonnaise over the past year, Otto stared at the
meteor with a look of horror. “Is the entire Natsuki family insane?” he whispered.

 

“It’s— Well—” Garfiel tried to stand up for his Captain, but found himself unable to form the
necessary words to defend the thought of someone drinking a cup of the condiment like a
glass of milk. “…Sorry, Captain,” he finally said, voice somewhere between revolted and
painfully apologetic.

 

“—Lady Anastasia?” Hetaro prodded, looking both curious and worried at her sudden
sobriety.

 

“What is it?” Tivey asked. He sounded more worried than curious.

 

“…Remember when we first moved here from Kararagi,” Anastasia said after a moment.
“And a few days after, you three missed daisukiyaki so much, ya said ya couldn’t go on
without it?”

 

[Fried chicken with mayo. Salad with, of course, mayo. Gyoza and fries and dessert
all with mayo. When you’re troubled, add mayo. If you’re bored, add mayo. —As a proud,



natural-born Mayo Lover, I live by this code of conduct, and yet for me it’s been a whole
month without my essential nutrient, my veritable soulmate…!]

 

“Oh,” Mimi said. Neither her nor her brothers looked quite so amused anymore.

 

“Ah,” Crusch said quietly. “I get it, too.”

 

Ferris turned away slightly, his mirth about the situation having abruptly drained away.
Ricardo felt similarly awkward. After all, that sort of despair was a little too personal to make
fun of, wasn’t it?

 

Felt grimaced, feeling something unpleasant. Next to her, however, Rachins had a very
strange look on his face. He both related to it deeply and didn’t relate at all: after all, hadn’t
he at least parted ways with his family by choice? Subaru’s situation was worse, because at
least Rachins had been able to make that decision for himself — but at the same time, at least
Subaru hadn’t been the one to blame.

 

“Lady Anastasia,” Julius clarified softly. “You’re saying that this is really about…”

 

“He’s homesick,” Anastasia confirmed quietly. “And unlike with us…”

 

Unlike with her, Ricardo, the Pearlbatons, and Kararagi, Subaru would likely never be able to
go back home again.

 

[Spirit wearing away, fingers trembling, tongue begging for oil and calories, eyesight
blurry and failing — these are the withdrawal symptoms of a Mayo Lover. They ruthlessly
eat away at my body, forcefully dragging me deep into a sea of agony…!]

 

Emilia swallowed, and found herself needing to avert her eyes: they were filling with tears
far too fast. With that context, wasn’t that monologue of Subaru’s just far too sad?

 



[“—And that is the White Lover, Mayonnaise.”]

 

[Subaru finished this overdramatic speech with a curt bow before promptly collapsing
back into his chair.]

 

[“So…” After a long moment of trying to digest — this — Emiilia crossed her arms.
“Basically, you’re quibbling over a condiment you liked?”]

 

Emilia flinched.

 

Garfiel noticed. “Lady Emilia,” he murmured. “You couldn’t have known.”

 

Otto pressed his lips together. That was right. That was right — because even now, Subaru
wasn’t telling anyone the real truth about what he was going through. He wished he could
punch Subaru in the face again for that, but alas.

 

[“Emilia-tan, you just don’t understand!!” Subaru slammed his fists into the table in a

“SUBARU!” Julius snapped.

 

Ferris snorted, albeit a little more subdued than before. “I can’t believe that spirit is putting
up with that,” he snickered.

 

[“To a Mayo Lover, even a day without mayonnaise is a glimpse of hell itself. And I’ve
suffered twenty…” He paused, and then corrected himself. “No, a whole week of it.”]

 

The entire room flinched violently at that correction. Ferris’ small smile slipped away once
more.

 



Otto really, really wanted to punch Subaru in the face again for this one.

 

[“A normal person would’ve gone mad by now. It’s only because of my inhuman mental
fortitude that I’ve survived up until now, but… I’m at my limits.”]

 

Someone hissed loudly. Otto buried his face in his hands.

 

In the present, Subaru wished he had been just a little more careful with his words.

 

[“A-Aren’t you just exaggerating? About going mad, and…”]

 

Emilia scowled. The idea of doubting Subaru’s agony, even for a moment…!

 

It didn’t matter how ridiculous it sounded on the outset. From now on, she would accept any
strife or wound he voiced to her with an open hand and an open heart. And if he couldn’t tell
her everything, for whatever reason it may be, then she would make do with the little that he
could bring himself to say.

 

[“If I was acting, would my hands and feet be trembling like this…?” Subaru moaned.
“Please believe me, Emilia-tan. Without mayonnaise, my body can’t survive.”]

 

Normally, Julius would have rolled his eyes. Now he just felt bad.

 

Subaru had a tendency to exaggerate his woes for humorous effect, but that didn’t mean the
pain wasn’t real on some level or other. And the pain of homesickness for a place to which
you would never be able to return…

 

His hometown had been flooded, and himself the only survivor. It wasn’t the same thing, he
knew, but Julius also knew the pain of missing his mother’s home-cooked meals far, far too
well.



 

[It’s commonly said that the oils in mayonnaise are akin to pure endorphins, Subaru
declared solemnly. Consuming this substance channels the purest of pleasures directly to
the brain, giving birth to the Mayo Lover. Thus, Roswaal’s guess is very close to the mark:
to myself, quitting mayonnaise causes a strain not unlike withdrawal symptoms…!]

 

Emilia remembered feeling very taken aback by his uncharacteristic seriousness about
something that sounded so very silly, especially when Subaru had always seemed to maintain

Felt could only shake her head, watching as the silver-haired half-elf fell completely into the

[“Well, even without mayonnaise, food is still delicious, very delicious even,” Subaru

thing that tastes like bread, and this soup-like liquid, that bowl of pseudo-salad, coupled
with a dubiously water-ish beverage, it all tastes delicious, incredibly delicious. But—”
He cradled his head in his hands. “It isn’t mayonnaise.”]

 

"Thing that tastes like bread?" Garfiel repeated.

 

"Soup-like liquid?" Mimi frowned.

 

"Bowl of pseudo-salad?" Wilhelm winced.

 

"Dubiously water-ish beverage?" Rachins cringed.

 

Everything being just a little bit off, to the point where even the most simple of things tasted
just a little to the left… Old Man Rom grimaced. It was really no wonder that Subaru had
succombed to such potent homesickness, if even THAT was different.



 

"Subaru…" Julius trailed off. He wasn't really sure what to do, here. Should he try to
replicate that taste that seemed lost between worlds? Should he search for new and interesting
things that would not have appeared in this boy's hometown at all? Should he simply offer a
shoulder, if Subaru ever felt like he needed it? They wouldnt be here forever, so when they
got out of here, what should he…?

 

[“It’s all prickly—” Puck complained, now trapped between Subaru’s right hand and
his head. And yet Subaru, lost deep in his sorrow, could not hear him.]

 

Julius was going to strangle that boy the moment he could get his hands on him.

 

[The greed of man knows no limits, Subaru reflected solemnly. Since coming to this
world, my only desire was for these peaceful days to continue. To stand at Emilia’s side, to
be surrounded by happy, smiling faces, to live each day peacefully and uneventfully.]

 

That was a nice desire, really. Crusch couldn’t fault anyone for having such a peaceful life as
their greatest wish, although she did have some concerns about some of the faces that he was
content about filling that space. But she didn’t see a problem with wanting more than that,

hometown once again.

 

Ferris leaned backwards, uncomfortable. He didn’t know why he was uncomfortable,
however, and that made him feel all the more frustrated.

 

[Having desperately clawed beyond times of pain and despair, my inner NEET dreamed
only of peace…]

 

That word again. Ricardo's frown deepened. Just what was it, and why did Subaru define
himself as…?

 

[But after overcoming crisis after crisis and reaching these precious days, I’m
overwhelmed by an insatiable hunger, screaming “it’s not enough!” —Disgusting. This



ruinous human greed, is utterly disgusting.]

 

“Ah…” Reinhard smiled awkwardly. Uneasily. “I… I don’t think there’s anything wrong with
wanting food you like, Subaru,” he said tentatively. He felt like he had maybe missed

Frederica just sighed. All those dramatics… Really, Subaru could be such a little boy
sometimes. It was charming, in an annoying sort of way.

 

That attitude did remind Beatrice of someone from a long, long time ago. Not enough, never
enough, constantly striving for more and more and more…

 

Her heart squeezed painfully in her chest.

 

[Aren’t I supposed to be satisfied with these peaceful days? Those which I so desired, and
then finally grasped?]

 

Felt scoffed. “Supposed” to be satisfied, what a ridiculous assertion. If you were then you

Not that it was relevant to the desire for something like a condiment, of course, but Rom had

most mature people he’d met in the long, long years of his life.

 

It would be easier if Subaru were the type to be satisfied by peaceful days. But unfortunately,

[Satisfied with this gift, can’t I just sink back into sloth and complacency?]



 

“N-No…?” Wilhelm said that in an attempt to be supportive, but he was so confused that it

Otto rolled his eyes. “Slothful,” “complacent” — those were two words that didn’t describe
Subaru even the slightest bit, whatever Subaru himself might declare.

 

[“—No. Absolutely not.” That voice doesn’t sound like my own at all, but it is… My own

Mimi leaned forward, eyes sparkling. That was right. That was right: if he wanted something,
then he would need to reach out and grab it! Wasn’t that what Boss Lady had always said?!

 

Rachins’ eyebrow had raised up and up and up, and now it was just about at his hairline. With

overdramatic?

 

[Advance, advance, advance— Toward an insatiable greed.]

 

Tivey could already feel a headache coming on. Grimacing, he rubbed at his temples.

 

[Onward, onward, onward— past the coveted days I strived to claim, go forth beyond and
aim for more.]

 

Hetaro looked from his older sister to his younger brother, between excitement and

[Thus, my pursuit continues, Subaru concluded silently. After escaping the endless loop of

Emilia swallowed. Even before he had opened his eyes that first morning in the manor, she

She couldn’t really forget that. She knew that Subaru didn’t want her to linger on that

Garfiel shifted uneasily. He had always loved stories of heroes, but the way that Subaru had

[“I was aimless, goalless, lacking a purpose in life,” Subaru declared. “But now, this is
my new dream… That is, to bring mayonnaise to this world. What’s, wrong, with,

[To bring the [white fairy] to the dinner table, that is my new purpose…!]

 

“It…” Rem felt so completely lost. “It is…?”

 

Ram just sighed. Subaru wanted so little, but the little he did want were things he desired

Anastasia held back a laugh. Recreating a favorite meal was such a simple goal, really. But
Subaru’s desires always were so very simple, weren’t they? Most importantly, simple or not,

Subaru could only turn away, humiliation coloring his face a brilliant hue. Of all the

[“Understood,” Rem declared, her eyes sparkling. “Subaru-kun’s request, please leave

“Ah?” Reinhard tilted his head.

 

Felt snorted. “Dunno why ya look so surprised by that,” she said, leaning her chin against her

[“In the first place, the task of managing the manor’s kitchen falls to Rem,” Ram was

Old Man Rom chuckled. Emilia and her obsession with favors and non-favors, Subaru and

[“You…” Subaru’s wet eyes looked upwards towards Rem. “You will do this with me,
Rem!”]

 

[Lately, she‘s been going out of her way to fulfill absolutely any request I ask of her,

Emilia’s eyes widened. “Subaru?!”

 

“Ah—” Subaru face turned red. It was a different quality than the flustered scarlet that had
become a common sight however: this was the hue of genuine shame. “I…” he managed.
“Rem, I—”

 



“It’s fine, Subaru,” Rem answered quickly. “Rem is the one who offered first, remember? I’m
sure that I was thrilled to do something like that for you. Don’t feel sorry for taking

Subaru slowly closed his mouth again, and Rem turned back to the meteor.

 

…So Subaru WAS capable of something like that, then. For some reason, that made Rem feel
more relieved than anything else.

 

“—Ah?” Wilhelm raised an eyebrow. Subaru…had planned to take advantage of Rem’s guilt
and affection?

 

…Wilhelm had promised to give him grace, at the very start, and that promise was still in

once.

 

Putting such judgements aside completely, however… Just how desperate had Subaru been
for a taste of home?

 

Subaru should be taking advantage of people more often, really: that was what Anastasia
thought. People took advantage and were taken advantage of, as was the way of the world.
Subaru allowed himself to be taken advantage of all the time, so wasn’t it only right to do
some taking of his own?

 

Especially because the opportunity to give the person you cared about something you knew
they truly, genuinely wanted for their own sake… Anastasia wondered if Subaru realized

[“Let us do it, Subaru-kun,” Rem declared, spreading out her arms. “Now, about the
recipe…”]

 



[“—eh?” Subaru said.]

 

The theater screeched to a halt.

 

[“—eh?” Rem said.]

 

Everyone turned towards the meteor. Aside from those belonging to the individuals who had
been present that day, equal looks of disbelief could be seen spreading across every face in

[And like that’s facing each other, Rem and Subaru froze solid, jaws slacked open and

“…You’re kidding,” Felt said flatly, breaking the silence of the theater. “After all that— Big
Bro. Big Bro, you are KIDDING.”

 

Subaru shrugged, a sheepish look on his face. Otto groaned and buried his face in his hands.

 

[“It’s too heavy—” Puck protested, still squashed between Subaru’s hand and the

Julius gritted his teeth at the sight. Subaru…!

 

Mimi could only giggle at the look on the knight’s face. Her two brothers sighed with odd,

[“‘Oh, my body can’t survive without it,’ he says,” Ram teased him later, as the two of

Old Man Rom groaned softly, slowly shaking his head with amused exasperation. Ram

(Though if Subaru continued to behave that brazenly towards the Beast of the End, Julius was

[“I won’t deny that. But as I was saying, do you perfectly understand your favorite

[“Ram’s favorites are everything Rem makes. And since Rem knows the recipes, Ram

Garfiel huffed with amusement. This usual banter between Ram and Captain, something that

“Well,” Frederica chuckled. “You went out of your way to learn your beloved sister’s recipe

[In contrast to my abnormally slow pace, retrieving the silverware, Ram transfers the

Ram frowned. “Of course I did,” she said, almost in disbelief. “What other behavior could

But Subaru could have expected any sort of dishonorable reaction to his injured self, couldn’t

“Finally, he jumped.”

 

[Objectively, this routine is terribly inefficient, but simple chores like this are part of my

Ram swallowed, thinking of Rem and her needless suffering brought by her guilt over a

But—

 

“My sister is too kind.”

 

But Rem hadn’t done anything but had a fleeting thought brought about by the worthless
adults in their hidden village: a hidden thought that she had immediately regretted and

much, much more than humor a simple fleeting thought, and there were some actions in this

“You really should have just rested,” Julius muttered, frowning. “After being injured like

If it had been Joshua, Julius wouldn’t have allowed him to refuse bedrest for at least a week.

“Stupid, stubborn little boy,” Mimi muttered. “—Don’t pretend you’re any better, though,
Julius.”

 



Julius didn’t hear her.

 

[Originally, Rem grandly declared herself as my aide, Subaru recalled with amusement.
But since she manages roughly ninety percent of the work around the manor she was
instantly rejected, and Ram openly volunteered in her stead. Rem’s absence from her usual
work would be a massive blow to the daily upkeep, after all…]

 

“Ya think she’d be aware of something like that,” Anastasia muttered, looking a little sour. “If

But she supposed that was the consequence of the disease known as inferiority: it blinded a
person to their true place in their environment, leaving them unable to act as their own best
selves as a result.

 

Crusch frowned. She had been thinking something similar, but Anastasia was being far too
harsh, wasn’t she? Rem was just a girl, after all.

 

[“If only she was more self-aware about that,” Subaru lamented with a sigh as he wiped

[Ram doesn’t slack off, but there‘s an undeniable difference in ability. And yet Rem’s self-

Emilia exhaled slowly. She would be lying, if she said that she didn’t understand the trap of

That was an accurate observation of the young maid, yes. Wilhelm let out a sigh. It was one

Though considering what he already knew would happen to the maid onscreen in just a little

Rem grimaced. She couldn’t say she approved of that pathetic sort of attitude, no.

 

[Her recent praise-seeking behavior could be seen as a sort of progress…]

 

Felt grimaced. “That’s not…”

 

Crusch was thinking something similar: that such an assumption wasn’t really true. With her
still demanding the validation of those around her instead of summoning it from within her
own soul, Rem’s core problem remained the exact same as before.

 

…Perhaps it was still progress in her reaching for what she thought she needed as opposed to
suffering in silence. She only hoped that the girl would improve further as she went forth.

 

[“Then again, the 24/7 barrage of [How is it?], [Did Rem do well?], [It isn’t strange, is
it?], [Is it tasty, Subaru-kun?], [Rem doesn’t mind being praised, yes?], [Praise me,

Rem cringed at the very thought. She couldn’t tell whether it was more out of stress at the
idea of being placed in such a position herself or embarrassment at the thought of herself
putting on such a display.

 

[I myself am allowing it and all, but the weight with which Rem has been leaning on me
lately is immense and crushing…!]

 

Anastasia scowled. All that talk about wanting to help Subaru recover, and it seemed that she

“A—” Garfiel winced. “Ah.”

 

He— He hadn’t done anything like that to Captain, right? He had been helpful ever since
they’d made up, right? Subaru hadn’t ever felt like Garfiel was…

 

Well. Even if Subaru couldn’t be trusted to answer him honestly, there was a good chance
that Garfiel was going to find out.

 

(He refused to allow himself to dread that eventuality: if he had done something to someone,
then he would have to take responsibility for it. There was nothing more to it than that.)

 

Otto glanced at Garfiel. Then he went back to watching the meteor. He didn’t really know

[After keeping to herself for so long, Rem is like an explosion. I just hope that, like an

Crusch winced. And all this while Subaru was still recovering — and from the very injuries
he gained whilst rushing to save her life, no less! That was…

 

Well. She hoped that Rem would indeed settle down a little bit. “High-maintenance girl”

Ferris cuddled closer to his Lady, oddly self-conscious. He didn’t know what he was feeling.

 

In many ways, Rem was a particularly ugly sort of mirror. He couldn’t help but resent her for
that, and at the same time he found himself yearning for her success. If she succeeded, after

[Be that as it may, I can’t just bluntly shake Rem off, Subaru reflected. Especially since…]

 

“…Ah,” Felt said, watching a light blush spread across Subaru’s face. “So, this is when that
started.”

 

Rachins shifted nervously. He’d known from the start about Subaru’s feelings for that
woman, as had everyone else, but…

 

Well. He wasn’t sure how he felt about those feelings anymore. It certainly wasn’t
amusement, not now that he knew everything that had preluded them.

 

For Ricardo and Ferris, this was as good an opportunity as any to pick on Subaru once more.
It said something that both of them stayed silent. —That, more than anything, caught
Subaru’s attention.

 

“Guys…?” he called over, looking both worried and confused. Nobody really knew how to
respond, and so his call went unanswered.

 

[“...That child’s stubborn inferiority complex is dyed straight into the wool. It must be
from our childhood, when Ram was a bit too much of a prodigy.”]

 

[“Isn’t it a bit much to call yourself a prodigy, especially in the past tense? How big-
headed does someone need to be to make a claim like that?”]

 

Old Man Rom shivered slightly as he remembered the look in that infant’s eyes, and the sheer
power that had emitted from her horn in that moment of truth. If anything, Ram was being
incredibly humble with that sort of understatement.

 

Subaru grimaced awkwardly, thinking something similar. He’d never, EVER say it out loud,
lest one of the twins hear him, but it was a bit of a shame that Ram hadn’t been able to keep



that incredible gift of hers, wasn’t it?

 

“Wasn’t your fault,” Felt muttered. “You weren’t anything but yourself.”

 

No, the real problem had been those foolish adults who couldn’t look past their own noses to
see who was standing directly before their eyes. Ridiculous, just ridiculous.

 

[“If Ram was still in her prime, everything above Barusu’s neck would be gone by
now…”]

 

Rem flinched violently. She wasn’t the only one. “R-Ram!” she cried. “Why would you…?!”

 

Ram hissed. She hadn’t meant it, of course. But just how many times had she said something
so horrifically, horrifically reckless…?!

 

(She had aimed for his neck, hadn’t she? She’d aimed for his neck, and then he had bled out
in the grass from a mangled throat. Why did she have to have specified his neck?)

 

[“Honestly,” Ram sighed wearily. “Why does Ram have to hang her hopes on a man like
Barusu.”]

 

[Subaru simply tilted his head, as if asking her what she meant by that.]

 

Glancing at the present, scandalized version of Ram’s little sister, Frederica was pretty sure
she understood quite well. After all, though she may not remember Rem, she had still known
Ram for many years.

 

[“Up until now…” With a side-glance, Ram shot him a particularly disgusted look. “All
that existed in Rem’s world was Ram, Roswaal-sama, and the manor. While Emilia-
sama and Beatrice-sama were in her scope as well, she probably didn’t attach much
importance to them. As for anyone else, all the more.”]



 

“—! Hey!” Frederica squawked. Ram pretended not to hear her.

 

[“Hmm, yeah,” Subaru noted. “Rem does seem to have that kind of narrow-
mindedness.”]

 

[That narrow-mindedness also explains why she rashly jumps to conclusions, he added
silently, lost in thought. Secluded from the world, Rem resolves her problems internally,
deciding everything by herself. —As a victim of that dangerous thought process, I know
this all too well…]

 

Everyone went still at the reminder.

 

It wasn’t like any of them had ever been able to forget, but… It was all too easy to think that
Subaru himself had forgotten, sometimes.

 

(Would that be a mercy or yet another cruelty in a sea of cruelties? Nobody there was really
sure.)

 

[Looking back, I can only lament my poor conduct from that time.]

 

Everyone sucked in a breath as one.

 

“Subaru…” Emilia trailed off. Just what was she supposed to say?

 

Subaru met her gaze with eyes firm. “It WAS my fault,” he declared. “It was entirely my
fault. Don’t— Don’t try to blame anyone else for an outcome that was my own doing. That’s
not fair.”

 

Nobody tried to argue this time. They just stared back at him in silence.



 

Rem wasn’t even surprised anymore. She turned back to the meteor. Subaru would always
defend her, even when she was at her worst, even when she had done the unforgivable. …It
was for that exact reason that Rem could not consider him a reliable source for how she
should be feeling about any of this.

 

Ram exhaled slowly. Subaru — was someone she cared for deeply, he truly was. And
because he was someone important to her, she could not allow herself to follow such simple
logic that would convenience her at the sake of the boy she had wronged so thoroughly.

 

—They’d talk about it later. Now wasn’t the time.

 

[“What are you staring at Ram for?” her old self asked coldly.]

 

[“Why don’t you figure it out for yourself, Nee-sama,” Subaru teased, flippantly
brushing the truth of what he had been thinking about aside with a crude insinuation.]

 

Julius remembered how Reinhard had described him, when the three of them had first come
together in the throne room. “A boy who always tries to make a bad first impression…” he
murmured aloud. Was there any merit to that strategy?

 

—No, he didn’t think so. All this puffing up and brushing off was frivolous, and the facade
that the boy often put on in an attempt to seem cool when he was nervous was, at best,
annoying. Julius liked Subaru most when he behaved like himself.

 

Ram had known even then that he was putting on an act in order to save face. She hadn’t
pressed him on it, of course. That had been her idea of kindness.

 

…Should she have pressed him further? Could such consideration really be called kindness at
all, or was it yet another way for her to fall into convenience at Subaru’s expense?

 



[“Stop looking at Ram with those perverted eyes. We’re the same in terms of looks, so
just do what you want with Rem instead.”]

 

Old Man Rom choked. “Little lady!”

 

Rem simply rolled her eyes. Her sister had quite the absurd sense of humor, didn’t she…?

 

[“That beautiful, sisterly love of yours isn’t beautiful at all, is it!”]

 

Ram chuckled slightly. A person as goodhearted as Subaru — who would become appalled at
the very idea of such a thing — that was the only audience that would make such a foul joke
funny. Indeed, the very idea of Subaru attempting to harm her baby sister was just absurd.

 

(Tivey and Hetaro exchanged horrified looks. Even as a joke, neither of them would ever
even think of…!)

 

(Anastasia sighed. Those two could be so overprotective sometimes — a reality made even
more ridiculous by the fact that Mimi easily outclassed them both.)

 

[“Well, putting that aside for now…” Ram skillfully ignored him, walking forward to
swipe the cloth out of his hand and usurp his role in their daily chores.]

 

“—Oh,” Garfiel said, finally realizing what it was that Ram had seen. Emilia simply smiled

Crusch’s eyes softened. So she had noticed.

 

It was comforting, in a way. If Subaru wasn’t going to look after himself, then Crusch would
rather like for him to be surrounded by people who knew to keep an eye on him.

 



(Her hand rubbed circles into Ferris’ back. She didn’t even realize what she was doing.)

 

[Ah. Subaru’s internal monologue suddenly filled with guilt. My arm gave out from
exhaustion some time ago. I’d tried to keep talking as an excuse for a break, but I guess
she saw right through me…]

 

[In response to her consideration, all he could do was sheepishly turn away.]

 

“Are you kidding me…?” Felt sighed. But of course he was serious. The guy had done all
that work, only to get embarrassed about how much effort he had put into it all. Ridiculous.

 

“Men are ridiculous,” Anastasia muttered. “Feeling the need to show off their strength all the
time like that…“

 

It drove her up the wall to no end to see boys throwing themselves at problems again and
again until they broke, when they could just as easily have surrendered their foolish pride and
allowed someone else to help them in their time of need. Ricardo, Tivey, Hetaro — even
Julius was like that sometimes, and Anastasia was certain that it was going to be the death of
her one of these days.

 

Only vaguely aware of his Lady’s general frustration, Julius pressed his lips together in
agreement. Subaru really should have just been resting and recovering.

 

[“So,” Subaru said, finally giving in and allowing her to work while he rested his
injured self. “What was that thing you were talking about?”]

 

[“Asking for an answer that you already know, Ram thinks that’s quite malicious.”]

 

Old Man Rom snorted. “It’s in poor taste for ya to go acting like that when YOU are the one
who brought up the topic, missy.”

 



Ram turned to Rom with an icy glare that made him recoil. “Don’t call Ram by that cursed
nickname, you foolish old man.”

 

“Alright, alright! I’m sorry!”

 

[“Wouldn’t it be bad if we misunderstand each other? After all, it’s an established fact
that I’m an oblivious guy who couldn’t read emotions to save his life. I’m Round
Table class.”]

 

[Ram let out a long sigh.]

 

“Round Table class…?” Anastasia murmured. A synonym for a “jack of all trades,” perhaps
— though she was rather curious about its origin.

 

[“Rem’s small, narrow world,” Ram elaborated. “Like a contamination, Barusu forced
his way into it. If that contamination rampages enough, the walls of that child’s small
world might push out just a bit. So dreams a beautiful girl named Ram.”]

 

[“Careful,” Subaru teased. “That act of yours is starting to resemble me a bit too
much.”]

 

Ferris snorted. “Nyew do have to watch out,” he teased. “Subaru-kyun is the type who rubs
off on others far too easily, isn’t he~?”

 

Normally Ram would respond with a huff, a snide comment, and a jab Subaru’s way. Now
her mouth felt far too dry for something like that.

 

[“Also, those dreams or whatever, don’t dump them onto me like that. I only do what I
can, and sometimes I don’t even do that.”]

 



Anastasia actually snorted, a sound that surprised herself more than it did anyone else. Her
cheeks turned pink. “A-Ah…”

 

Crusch smiled at her, giggling in agreement. Felt just rolled her eyes.

 

Lady Anastasia had been taken aback by her unladylike outburst, but most everyone else was
too caught up at the absurdity of Subaru, of all people, describing himself in such a ridiculous
manner.

 

“You get involved in everything, Natsuki-san,” Otto muttered. Next to him, Garfiel was
snickering loudly. “Don’t you go pretending to be anything else.”

 

Ram turned away slightly. Really, she had no place asking anything of Subaru after…

 

She had never really had any place doing that after all, it turns out.

 

[My motto is “To do or not to do? If you can’t decide, then don’t do anything,” Subaru
reflected with a triumphant smirk as he boasted his uselessness. With that as my
personal creed, I’ve allowed countless potential events to slip past me.]

 

At that, Garfiel’s snickers graduated into full-bodied laughter. He wasn’t the only one: half
the audience had started cackling at such a ridiculous self-assessment.

 

“Of all people…” Emilia sighed. “You can be absolutely ridiculous sometimes, Subaru. You
know that?”

 

—Ricardo frowned. Subaru, of all people, describing himself like that?

 

…What had his life actually been like before he had come to Lugunica?

 



[“Hmph,” Ram huffed curtly. “Unable to abandon the village children, much less leave
Rem behind. And in the end, becoming a decoy to let Ram and Rem escape. Trying to

Rem giggled a little. Ram could only shake her head with a sigh. To this day, she was unclear

…Then again, he had pretended things were fine for so long and to such an extent that Ram

The thought sobered her. Subaru was a terrible liar, but she had been wrong: he was a

[“Stop spelling out my deeds!” Subaru exclaimed, crouching and furiously shaking his

“—Embarrassed?” Garfiel echoed, completely bewildered. “But…” But what was there for

“Weeell,” Ferris teased. “It wasn’t like we didn’t all knyow what sort of reckless, brash, silly
boy Subaru-kyun is, hmm~? Nya can’t fool us, nyew knyow!”

 

Subaru grimaced. Even after a year, he couldn’t help but feel like he was fooling all of them
jusf by sitting here and letting them watch his memory of those horrible, horrible events.
After all, to see them all in various stages of befuddlement at hearing Subaru state the honest

It WAS him, though, Crusch knew. After all, whether he wanted to accept it or not, it was
none other than Subaru who had done all those things in the face of those Ulgarm Wolves.
For better or for worse, he was the only one fit to take responsibility for it all.



 

[Though I managed to break out from the endless loops of death for the second time…
Subaru shuddered, goosebumps forming all over. Who is that crazy, hot-blooded youth?!]

 

“Sometimes I wonder that myself,” Julius muttered, thinking of the heart attack he would
likely sustain sooner rather than later because of this reckless boy. Reinhard just laughed.

 

Wilhelm couldn’t help but smile. That crazy and hot-blooded youth reminded him so much of
himself at that age, after all — but with the sort of wisdom his old self had never really
managed to obtain, even this late in life.

 

…Really, he had been blessed quite enough just to meet Subaru at all, hadn’t he?

 

[“For the cool and gallant Natsuki Subaru, it’s just unbecoming,” Subaru lamented. “If
I’d heroically taken care of everything myself, it’d be another story. But didn’t I just
blow black smoke everywhere and let Ros-chi handle the rest?!”]

 

Garfiel reeled back in his seat, blinking rapidly. “…What?!” he finally exclaimed, voice
dripping with disbelief.

 

[“Well, logically speaking, that is how it was.”]

 

[“I knew it! I tried so hard too, damnit!”]

 

“That’s…” Having once agreed with that statement, even in jest, Ram now found herself
nearly struck speechless by the unfairness of that declaration. “That’s— Subaru—”

 

Otto gritted his teeth. “Natsuki-san,” he muttered. “Natsuki-san, you stupid, stupid little…”

 



Frederica’s upper lip wobbled, and she had to turn away. He really had tried so hard, hadn’t
he? So…why did it feel like he couldn’t even see it?

 

[After countless loops, that’s the end result.]

 

Subaru huffed, his new outside view having put into perspective how ridiculous that idea
was. “Countless…” he muttered, too quietly for anyone else to hear him. “It was four. It was
only four…”

 

—Across the room, Crusch frowned, her worry deepening. Had it really felt like countless
loops to Subaru after just four deaths within the manor’s walls?

 

It wasn’t like she could blame him. Death was the sort of experience a soul was only built to
handle the one time, before being mercifully cleansed by Od Laguna. But for him to describe
it in such a way — it wasn’t shameful, not even close, but it did fill her with a quiet sort of

[In reaching that result, I undoubtedly struggled, Subaru reflected miserably. Yet, with no
one aware of my suffering, everyone probably thinks “Oh, he just got involved by chance
or something.”]

 

What did that matter? Felt wanted to bop him over the head for that stupid comment. What
the hell did it matter, if he had gotten involved by chance or by planning? All that mattered
was that he had gotten involved, could he really not see past his nose enough to understand
even that much?!

 

[Moreover, without landing a decisive blow of any sort, my role amounts to “that guy who
was just sort of there by chance.” And most of all—]

 

Wilhelm opened his mouth, but someone else beat him to it this time.

 

[“Barusu was there.”]



 

“E-Eh?” Tivey startled.

 

Ricardo blinked, looking very taken aback. “Is that—?”

 

With a similar look on his face to that of the Mercenary Captain, Old Man Rom suddenly
looked rather alert.

 

…Wilhelm closed his mouth again, feeling oddly satisfied.

 

[Ram was the one who had interrupted him, of course. But unlike most times she spoke
with him, her voice now was soft and gentle, her usual cynicism and colloid hatred
replaced by genuine warmth and kindness.]

 

[“Sometimes that alone can save someone,” she chided. “You should know that.”]

 

“—That’s exactly right,” Felt said. Her voice was odd. “Doesn’t matter jack shit if ya have
the ability to save people and never do anything with it. Trying your best with what you’ve
got… That’s the important part, not the parts of yourself you never had any control over.”

 

“Indeed,” Crusch agreed quietly. “How a person conducts themselves is what says the most.
Anything else is superfluous, as far as I’m concerned.”

 

“Ah—” With everyone’s attention suddenly turned towards his present self, Subaru found the

laugh. “It’s okay, guys, I— It’s not a lie that I didn’t do much, in the end. I can’t be delusional
about that, you know?”

 

Emilia swallowed. Didn’t do much…?

 



Those were those old habits of his shining through again, she supposed. Just how many of
them remained, even after all this time?

 

“Ah— Emilia!” Subaru had noticed her sorrow before she could mask it, and to her great
guilt he began to panic. “I-It’s really not that bad,” he insisted. “I’ve come to terms with it,
you know?! I— I don’t HAVE to be the guy who does everything. That thing about lifting
quain stones, remember that?”

 

“No one can lift a quain stone alone.” Garfiel knew that idiom well, and he had carried it in
his heart every day since Captain had freed him from those chains he had woven for himself
with his own toe hands. But at the same time—

 

“You died, Captain,” he whispered. “This isn’t…”

 

How could he say that he hadn’t actually done anything?

 

“—Ya know,” Anastasia said suddenly. “There’s a story I heard once a long time ago in
Kararagi, about a princess who asked for donations from around the country.” Subaru
blinked, a little startled. “Have ya heard of it?”

 

“Uh…” The boy furrowed his brow, as if searching through his memory. “Ah…”

 

That was enough of an answer, and so the Merchant Princess continued.

 

“The rich men who had much to give donated hundreds of golden coins, scant fractions of
their immense wealth,” Anastasia said. Her voice was casual, but her eyes were decidedly
not. “But when the hyena boy who had nothing else to give offered a simple handful of
copper coins, it was he who was praised for the greatest contribution. Numerically it may not
have been all that much, but those little coins had meant so much more to the hyena boy than
those hundreds of gold coins had meant to any of the rich men combined, and so they had
been the most valuable gift of all.”

 



She wasn’t quite sure where she had heard that story before. But there was a lesson in there
that she thought was most important for the boy in front of her to internalize, and so she had
repeated it regardless. And in any case, he had already told her enough stories from his own
hometown that she felt that she would quite like to start returning the favor.

 

[“—Now that I think about it,“ Subaru fretted, callously brushing aside Ram’s

Rom could’ve done that! I’m in despair—!”]

 

“What a rude response!” Frederica exclaimed. Refusing Ram’s rare honesty and genuine

Wilhelm was chuckling. “Ahh,” he said with amusement. “Well, all young boys have their
moments, don’t they…?”

 

“I did worse, at his age,” Ricardo grinned. “Still, I’d say a reaction like that to the words of a
lady warrants a slap, eh…?”

 

“That’s most likely what comes next, yes,” Old Man Rom winced. He had gotten slapped
quite a few times in his youth himself.

 

Ferris was scowling. He felt too bitter to join in the teasing, and so he just lowered his gaze to
his feet. His tail lashed once behind him, and then fell still.

 

Most others in the theater were in similar states, annoyed or amused or somewhere in
between. Anastasia, however, was still focused solely on the Subaru that existed right now,

“That’s…” It was a familiar story, vaguely reminiscent of a Christian folktale Subaru thought
he recalled, but he shook his head. “That’s — not the sort of story I’d expect to hear from

“It’s not a perfect story, of course,” Anastasia dismissed. “It’s very naïve, first of all, and it

Subaru held her gaze for long enough for Anastasia to understand that he had heard her, and

(She refused to count that self-destructive curse of his as a golden coin, and refused even

sort of gesture that could mean the entire world.)

 

[Ram’s face fell into an unpleasant scowl as her words fail to reach Subaru, grieving
over his paltry achievements. Thus, she lets loose an explosive low kick, buckling his

Wilhelm sighed. It wasn’t like he could blame her for that reaction.

 

In the present moment, Ram flinched. She had never thought anything of it before, but after
—

 

“My sister is too kind.”



 

…Had she really needed to be so rough with him?

 

[“As expected,” Ram declared, looking annoyed enough to spit on him. “Hanging any
hope on a failure like Barusu is a lost cause.”]

 

Rem winced. “Isn’t that…?”

 

“Nah,” Felt muttered. “If Subaru acted like this all the time, then any shred of hope would be

Rem grimaced. Felt couldn’t help but grin back at her: that soft spot she’d developed for the

Emilia just watched with a cold, pained expression. Perhaps she wouldn’t have put it quite

[“So harsh!” Subaru got up, meeting her hard stare by snapping his fingers before

“Responding so positively only when being treated like that…” Otto muttered. “You really

“I won’t deny that, but Otto-bro sure ain’t one to talk!” Garfiel laughed.

 



Frederica just sighed, watching the three boys squabble. —Complications aside, it was nice

[“Expanding worlds or whatever, instead of relying on some stranger, you should do

“—Eh?” Crusch blinked.

 

[“Boasting about your [Clairvoyance] when you don’t even know the names of the local

Tivey tilted his head. “That…”

 

“…Ah,” Ricardo said. “He’s not wrong, is he?”

 

Of course he was right. Mimi rolled her eyes. Yet another way in which this self-proclaimed
older sister was entirely inadequate, wasn’t that right?

 

Felt sighed. “Reinhard’s old man has the same problem,” she muttered. “Calling himself the
Head of House Astrea when he hasn’t tended to his own lands in…”

 

Rachins sneered at the thought, and then he pushed it aside. He wanted to think about
Heinkel Astrea as little as he could.

 

(Across the room, Reinhard pretended not to hear either of them. That was either than
confronting them, when he didn’t know what it was that he could possibly say.)

 

[“…What are you—”]

 



[“You and Rem, your scopes are both too narrow,” Subaru declared. “All you two ever
do is look to each other for anything and everything. If you’ve gotta be together, instead

Julius hesitated. To walk alongside instead of stare directly at the person you admired the
most…

 

“Ya should listen to him, Jules,” Anastasia’s voice whispered. He startled slightly. “Natsuki-
san ain’t quite on your level when it comes to most things, but he’s definitely someone ya

“…I suppose he is,” Julius agreed quietly.

 

But still — wasn’t that advice the sort of thing that was easier said than done?

 

Wilhelm sat there in silence for a long moment, digesting the young boy’s words. Then he

[“How’s that?” Snapping his fingers and flashing a bright smile, Subaru struck his best

…Ferris smiled, just a little. Maybe that warranted some smidge of forgiveness.

 

Subaru was a stupid, stupid boy. But he was also genuine and insightful at the most surprising
of times, wasn’t he? Few people in this world were so full of surprises.

 

(Fourier’s beaming face flashed through his mind’s eye. The warmth of joyful affection and

[“Enough that it’s unimaginable for Barusu and the person who cried over a condiment

Julius chuckled a little at that. “She’s not wrong,” he teased. Subaru stuck his tongue out at

[Subaru’s laugh was oddly bitter. So harsh.]

 

Old Man Rom grimaced at the odd quality to that snicker. That “mayonnaise” really had

Made oddly uncomfortable by the sincerity in Subaru’s bitterness, Rachins couldn’t help but

[“Well…” Subaru glanced around the hall. “Let’s take our time with this. I’m sure Rem

“Subaru!” Crusch exclaimed, scandalized.

 

Old Man Rom barked out an incredulous laugh, abruptly shaken out of his solemn
reflections. “What a thing to say!” he crowed.

 

Emilia shook her head, hiding quiet giggles behind her hand.

 

“It’s not a very polite thing to tell someone,” Frederica grinned. “Even if it is true~”

 

[“Yes,” Ram said. Subaru had been teasing, but there was not a hint of bluffing in her
answer. “Ram hopes that day comes soon.”]



 

Frederica’s grin faltered. Around her, the amusement faded from the theater at Ram’s serious

—Though, Rem wondered if she would have done something like that little wind magic trick
