cruelly and mercilessly this world’s God plays with destiny. Oh, you thought you were safe?
Sorry, BAD END! I should have seen this coming—!]

 

How could he have seen this coming? He was just taking a bath — he had just been going to
take a bath, that was it! His coworker had told him that she’d ran him a bath, and so he went
to wash up because he worried he was unclean, and—

 

Julius had often found himself scolding Subaru for his reckless behavior since this
demonstration had begun, but why was it always moments like this — when he had clearly
not been at fault at all — that Subaru began to blame himself for not being careful?!

 

Perhaps Wilhelm could have found these dramatics funny, if a situation like this had
happened at another time, in another place, at the hands of some other person. But right now
—

 

Wilhelm’s hands squeezed the armrests of his chair until his knuckles turned white, his teeth
grinding themselves as he fought back a scream.

 

Rom could only cringe as he watched everything unfold. The silence of the theater only made
it all feel even worse.

 

[Subaru finally managed to wipe his eyes and stare at the ceiling with the look of a
terrified wild animal, sprawled on the floor, but he was still struggling to breathe. I
don’t know what this is. I don’t know what’s happening. Maybe I can call for help? But
what if it’s a trap? What if I call for help and just lead my savior to their grave?! But if I
don’t, then surely the perpetrator will come and finish me off—!]

 

Even in the midst of what he thought was a surprise attack to suffocate him in the bath,
Subaru couldn’t help but put others first. Ricardo wanted to be impressed, but really he
couldn’t feel anything but terror that he could suffocate right there on the floor because he
couldn’t bring himself to just cry for help—!

 



Emilia had remembered this incident as a goofy, cheerful footnote during their more peaceful
times at the Manor. But now, listening to Subaru’s genuine terror— listening to his refusal to
call for help because it might put HER in danger—!

 

Emilia had to try very, very hard not to cry.

 

“—! Guys, you’re taking this way too seriously!” Subaru exclaimed. “I was being stupid!
Just look at me, willing about like that on the bathroom floor covered in mayonnaise. Isn’t
that ridiculous?! I was incapacitated in such a dumb way, and in any case I wasn’t actually in
danger—!”

 

“Captain…” Garfiel trailed off, eyes pained.

 

Maybe Garfiel should have been laughing at the idea of someone drowning in mayonnaise.
Maybe he should have been teasing Captain about what an embarrassing way to go that
would be. But it wasn’t funny, when Subaru really had died before — and by this same
culprit’s hand, no less. It wasn’t funny, when his thoughts echoed with genuine terror that this
time, too, might end with…

 

(Garfiel loved to tease his friends — his brothers most of all — but he had his limits
regarding what he could stomach. Mocking Subaru for…this…would cross a line. Even if
Subaru himself didn’t seem to see it.)

 

Otto didn’t say anything. He just watched, a cold look on his face.

 

[“If I die — hide my body for three days!” Subaru gasped, giving his last rites aloud in a
panic. “In that time — make preparations for— Hm?!”]

 

Beatrice frowned. That felt like a reference to a story Subaru had mentioned from his
hometown once or twice, of a man who let himself be killed before rising again on the third
day, intending to bear the sins of everyone else in the world.

 



…She wasn’t sure if she liked that comparison much.

 

[Suddenly, a particular sensation spread across his tongue. Viscous, oily, and above all
else, a hint of sourness—!]

 

Frederica couldn’t help but cringe at the thought of cleaning that bath after it had been filled
to the brim with mayonnaise. To be covered head to toe in it, meanwhile, was a horror she
couldn’t even imagine…!

 

[“Yes!” Subaru’s shouts for help quickly became garbled and muffled by his
predicament. And yet, as if she had been standing right outside all along, Rem dutifully
came rushing in. “Did you call for Rem, Subaru-kun?!”]

 

“—YOU NEARLY KILLED HIM!” Mimi snarled, eyes wild and frantic as she leaped to her
feet, shaking violently from head to toe. “You nearly— You nearly killed him AGAIN!
What’s wrong with you?!”

 

“Onee-chan!” Tivey objected, desperately pulling her back down. “Onee-chan, you’re not
exactly wrong, but—!”

 

Hetaro just sighed. From the looks of it, Rem didn’t even seem to be paying attention to
Mimi at all: she seemed far too caught up in her own horrified realizations of that exact same
thing.

 

[“How is it, the feeling of swimming in mayonnaise? Rem did her best to satisfy Subaru-
kun’s request. —Rem doesn’t mind being praised?”]

 

[It took Subaru a moment to respond. And when he finally did —]

 

{"ARE YOU AN IDIOT?!"]

 



Emilia let out a shuddering breath, and then forced herself to smile. They had decided that
they would maintain a sizable stock of mayonnaise after this incident, because it was tasty
and it would be nice if they always had some of it. But even with that fond memory to
comfort her…

 

“That really wasn’t very nice, Rem,” she murmured, her brow furrowed. “It really wasn’t…”

 

Ram wanted to defend her little sister, but she just couldn’t find the words for it this time.

 

—Having watched the entire scene in utter silence, Rem could only stare at her old self in
disbelief as she apologized profusely to an irate-looking blob-monster version of Natsuki
Subaru, who seemed to be attempting to scold her through the mayonnaise still covering him
from head to toe.

 

“R-Rem was, ah, a little traumatized after this,” Subaru said, trying to lighten the mood again
as he forced a laugh. “You were really good at making mayonnaise, but you never really did
get over that first impression, so Ram ended up taking over from then on. My attempt to use
mayonnaise to boost your self-esteem really did backfire…!”

 

Rem forced herself to laugh, even though she really didn’t see the humor in this situation at
all.

 

The theater was quiet for a long, long moment.

 

[“One, two, three, four! One, two, three, four—!”]

 

—Garfiel was the first to get over the shock of that uncomfortable scene enough to bark out a
more cheerful exclamation, doing his best to do his part in lightening the mood again.

 

“Radio calisthenics!” he crowed. “Ya got the entire Irlam Village involved in that, Captain?”

 



“He… He did it every morning,” Emilia confirmed. Slowly, she began to smile warmly
again. “As soon as he had recovered from the Wolgarm Incident enough, he was out there
every morning to play with the villagers. It was nice…”

 

“He still sometimes gets up and tries to head out to Irlam Village for radio calisthenics on
impulse, in fact,” Beatrice grumbled. “And he keeps dragging Betty with him, and then he
doesn’t remember that he’s far away in Miload Manor until he’s already out in the woods…”

 

Subaru chuckled, a somewhat sheepish look on his face.

 

[“Without this, I would lose out to Rem-san, who he sees every day…” Petra muttered
aloud.]

 

“—Eh?” Rem said aloud. “Lose to me?”

 

Ram snorted. She had teased him about it before, but she knew well and good that Subaru
would never see someone this much younger than him in a manner like that. The little girl
known as Petra had lost that particular battle from the very start.

 

(Though, Ram was not yet entirely certain whether or not she wanted her dear little sister to
WIN.)

 

So, it seemed that Petra had acknowledged Rem as her love rival — and a formidable one at
that. Wilhelm fought back a laugh, not wanting to diminish young Petra’s determination, but
he couldn’t stop his eyes from twinkling with amusement. That look on her face as she
thought of Rem’s natural advantage in time spent with their mutual crush was of a girl who
had recognized someone as her lifelong rival in love.

 

“Victory over Rem is the condition for my first love. It will be a fierce, hard-fought battle,
even for my cute and unrivaled self.” —Old Man Rom had the feeling that was the thought
going through Petra’s mind just then. He sighed, feeling a mix of amusement and exhaustion.
Youngsters were something else.

 



“I know,” Ram commiserated with the giant, huffing slightly.

 

“…I didn’t say anything.”

 

“You said enough.”

 

It went even deeper than the old man had realized. After all, though Ram knew that Petra saw
radio calisthenics as embarrassing, but she also knew that Petra had gone around waking up
all the adults in her village every morning, including her parents and Muraosa, until it
became a habit for all of them to wake up in time to do radio calisthenics with Subaru as part
of their morning routine. Really, nothing would ever keep that girl from giving something her
very best effort once she had decided upon it.

 

“‘It’s hard to be noticed by Subaru if you’re just cute,’ according to Petra,” Frederica recalled
with amusement. “‘Do not sit on your laurels, do not neglect efforts to improve yourself, and
do everything you can to know your enemy.’ That’s what she said.”

 

“'A character brimming with uncomplicated goodness and a kind personality,'” Ram
reflected quietly, her amusement fading. Rem blinked, turning to listen. “She never did think
his servant uniform suited him well—” Important, for a girl interested in clothes. “—and she
thought he made a terrible first impression, but his gentle soul was what won her over, she
says.”

 

Uncomplicated goodness, a kind and gentle personality… Rem thought such a description
was all too lacking. There were no words to describe what she had witnessed, when he had
extended a hand her way again and again even after all he had experienced at the other end of
her own.

 

“It’s a little sad,” Otto sighed, shaking his head with amusement. He could see Dyne and
Cain with stars in their eyes just behind her, and he already knew they didn’t stand a chance.
“Even with multiple boys floating after her…”

 

It seemed Petra had never been able to see any of her childhood friends as anything but
siblings, or any of the older men in the village as anything but older brothers and fathers.



Subaru had truly come about as her very first crush, and she had fallen hard and fast. —Otto
felt sorry for them, a little bit, but more than anything he couldn’t help but laugh at the
innocent expression of childhood playing out before his eyes.

 

Frederica giggled. “I feel a little bad for Meina, too,” she whispered, eyes shifting to a
similar-aged girl nearby. “Petra doted on her as a little sister for so long, but then Subaru-
sama came and stole all of her attention, and right when Meina had a little sibling on the
way…”

 

Come to think of it, Meina had been the one to write “I love you” on Subaru’s bandages. Of
course, she hadn’t meant it in the way that Petra likely would have, but Frederica wondered
how Petra would have reacted if that had come up in conversation. Perhaps she would need
to ask her later.

 

—Anastasia didn’t laugh.

 

If Petra’s ambitious desire was to win Subaru’s heart, then Anastasia could not laugh. Even if
she knew that Petra was too young for him, even if she knew that Subaru was smitten with
someone else, the fact remained that it was of great importance to Petra. And so, Anastasia
could not — would not — dismiss it with a laugh.

 

Instead, she silently praised that ambition shining in her eyes. The look of a calm mind, the
look of a clear head, the look of a naturally competitive personality that knew how to put up a
good fight, the look of a girl who had decided what she wanted and began to plan a way for
her hands to reach out and take it for herself… Anastasia could only look on with a great
sense of pride.

 

—Perhaps Subaru was a lost cause, but one day Petra would fall in love again. And when she
did, Anastasia had no doubt she would take the lessons she learned here and apply them to
their fullest to reach the summit that she craved so.

 

[“Alright, Victory!” Subaru crowed happily, finishing up radio calisthenics for the day.
“Let's gather! See, there's a reward for being here today!”]

 



“—A tato stamp?” Anastasia said aloud.

 

“Subaru carved a new tato stamp every day,” Emilia giggled. “He gave all the villagers a
little card, and then every time they participated in radio calisthenics, he’d stamp the stamp of
the day on their card. They always looked forward to seeing what the new design would be
each morning…”

 

There was nothing to be gained by collecting them, not really, but it had been a fun thing to
look forward to in that small village. —Petra was one of the people who loved the tato
stamps, but that was more because, for the most part, Petra loved everything that Subaru did.
Emilia couldn’t help but smile at the memory.

 

[“Oh, Petra, you did a great job of keeping your arms and legs moving this morning,”
Subaru greeted warmly.]

 

[“Hehe, really?” Petra giggled. “Was it cute? Was it cute?”]

 

It was no secret that Petra prided herself on being cute, Frederica thought with amusement.
But she was also a very cunning girl who would not be satisfied with relying on looks alone.
This was what had led to her applying to become a maid of the Mathers Estate, after all —
and Frederica already knew that it was the attitude that Petra carried with her while chasing
her first ever crush.

 

[“Oh, it was cute, it was cute!” Subaru agreed brightly. “And for such a cute Petra, I'll
give you a bonus, and…”]

 

[But just as he was going to stamp her card, Subaru’s hand slipped, and the tato stamp
fell to the ground.]

 

“Ah?!” Reinhard exclaimed, eyes widening. “Not the…!”

 



It was such a cute little stamp, after all, and Subaru had put such effort into it! If he were to
see it get destroyed…!

 

Next to him, Subaru couldn’t help but snort. “It’s just a tato stamp, Reinhard,” he teased,
even as his old self attempted to scramble after it. “I can probably make you one, if you’d
like.”

 

Reinhard was a little too late at stopping himself from visibly perking up. He coughed into
his fist, but Subaru’s laughing face let him know that the damage had been done. He sighed
with surrender, and then just said what Subaru already knew: “…I think I’d like that.”

 

[“…Yes. Don't panic.” Emilia’s voice answered his panicked scramble to pick it up
calmly, and a hooded figure reached for the tato stamp, easily picking it up and handing
it to him. “You're just scatterbrained.”]

 

“You’re one to talk, I supposed,” Beatrice huffed. Emilia was a notorious airhead, after all.

 

Otto sighed nearby. In that respect, Subaru and Emilia were one and the same. …There were
many respects where that was the case, really.

 

[“Who even says that these days?” Subaru teased.]

 

[“Don’t make fun of me.” Emilia poked his forehead lightly.]

 

It was far from a typical relationship between Lady and attendant. But as he watched them
tease each other gently with matching feelings of warmth and fondness (even if only one
party was looking at the other with the pinkness of romance in his eyes) Julius didn’t think he
could ever dare to describe it as anything but its own kind of wonderful.

 

Subaru scowled at him from across the theater. “I can already tell that you’re thinking
something annoying, jerk.”



 

[Petra was looking at the unfamiliar hooded, feminine figure with a look of suspicion, as
if wondering if there was such a person around Irlam Village. “Hey, Subaru…”]

 

[“—Mm, oh, oh, I'm sorry, I'm sorry,” Subaru shook himself, turning his attention back
to Petra as requested. “Okay, let's resume. Let's stamp it!”]

 

[And he stamped the participation card — but Petra wasn’t paying to the pattern left
behind at all.]

 

Anastasia started giggling at the suspicious look in Petra’s eyes, which were glued to
Subaru’s face. “‘Too happy,’ is what she’s thinking, hm?”

 

Rom could already feel the headache coming on. He stifled a groan: youngsters really were
something else.

 

[With a single motion, Petra let go of her card, making believe that the wind had
carried it right to Emilia’s feet.]

 

Mimi snorted. “Clumsy,” she teased.

 

Tivey batted her slightly. “She’s just a kid,” he scolded. “Don’t be mean, Onee-chan…”

 

Hetaro’s eyes remained on Petra’s calculating face. Had she thrown the card in that direction
just so she’d have an excuse to…?

 

[“…Huh?” Emilia said aloud. “You dropped this. Here."]

 

[And thus, Petra was given the chance to peer under her hood.]



 

“Ahhh,” Ricardo laughed, coming to the same conclusion as Hetaro. “Clever girl, ain'tcha?
She reminds me a bit of herself, Ana-bo!”

 

Anastasia swatted at him. “What have I said about calling me that?” she scolded. She said
this, but she herself couldn’t keep herself was smiling.

 

The dismay that swept across Petra’s face was the dismay of a girl who found herself facing a
new lifelong enemy on the battlefield of love — and one far more formidable than the last.
Felt nearly barked out a laugh at the sight of it, as though a battered soldier were seeing a
fresh enemy party enter the front lines.

 

Rachins huffed, feeling a little jealous. It wasn’t like little Petra was anything close to a babe,
but for Subaru to have multiple girls looking at him like that…!

 

It wasn’t that he was all that interested in chasing girls at the moment. But it’d be nice,
probably, to be the sort of guy that multiple girls would look at with eyes like that.

 

[“―?” Emilia tilted her head curiously at Petra’s wide-eyed expression. “What's
wrong?”]

 

“Ahh…” Wilhelm chuckled, correctly guessing Petra’s thoughts on the matter. “Another
opponent had entered the battlefield, hm?”

 

[Petra’s eyes darted between Subaru and Emilia, no doubt having correctly assessed
Subaru’s feelings for the silver-haired woman.]

 

Crusch frowned, titling her head. Petra liked Subaru, she understood that. Subaru liked
Emilia, she understood that as well. But why would that constitute Petra and Emilia
becoming enemies…?

 



Ferris watched Crusch’s face as she attempted to puzzle this out, and he couldn’t help
giggling. Cruschie was wise and intelligent and amazing in so very many ways, but when it
came to the subject of romance she had always been a little…

 

The similarities to her past self stung his heart just as much as they soothed his soul.

 

[“—Bleehh!” Petra stuck out her tongue, unable to find any other way to fight back
whilst struggling with her first love.]

 

The theater burst into uproarious laughter at the familiar, childish response.

 

“Petra!” Frederica snapped. Next to her, Garfiel was practically howling. Otto sighed,
suppressing his giggles as he shook his head.

 

[“Eh?!” Emilia exclaimed, Petra childishly declaring war on her as she snatched back
her participation card. “Why?!”]

 

In the present moment, Emilia found herself laughing alongside everyone else. She was
pretty sure she understood, now, what it was that had happened that day. At the time she had
been frightened that perhaps the young village girl had seen her as a half-elf with silver hair
even beneath her cloak, but now…

 

Really. She and Petra both, they could be so very silly sometimes.

 

[“Being cute is not enough to win,” Petra muttered, softly enough that neither Subaru
nor Emilia heard her as she left. “The world is a very big place…”]

 

Rem hadn’t laughed at all, and now she nodded somberly. In a world like this, she doubted
that cuteness alone could get one very far in life. Those were good words to keep in mind.
That went for herself — but it also went for Subaru, who was very, very cute indeed…

 



Ram sighed. She could already tell that her cute little sister was thinking something absurd.
Some things would never change, perhaps.

 

Subaru leaned his chin against the palm of his hand, smiling softly. He would never see her as
anything but a child, he knew, but Petra really was an adorably precocious little girl. He
hoped she would find someone her age who knew to appreciate her properly someday.

 

“—If he doesn’t, I’ll be sure to string him up by his ankles!” he said aloud, a streak of
indignant anger flaring up at the thought. “No delinquent is gonna get away with mistreating
little Petra like that, not on my watch!”

 

Beatrice sighed. Her contractor was being ridiculous again, she supposed. But, in fact, that
was one of the things that made Subaru so very, very cute…

 

So, perhaps she could let it slide.

Chapter End Notes

As a quick disclaimer, I will say that the original [Mayonnaise Scramble] side story
ended like this:

*

[“How is it, the feeling of swimming in mayonnaise? Rem did her best to satisfy
Subaru-kun’s request. ----Rem doesn’t mind being praised?”]

[/Praise me, praise me,/ her smiling face seems to say.]

[Standing up, Subaru uses the towel to wipe off the rest of his mayonnaise-laden body.
And, returning Rem’s innocent smiling face with his own smile,]

[*“ARE YOU AN IDIOT?!”*]

[In the early hours of the morning, Subaru’s yells boom throughout the bathhouse.]

[Seeing his soulmate, mayonnaise, wasted so callously, Subaru feels a rage like no other.
Eventually, an oversleeping Ram awakens as well. At her elder sister’s hands, an
apologetically kneeling Rem suffers a lecture of unspeakable length, unspeakable
severity, and /unspeakable violence./]



[“It’s tasty, so it’d be nice if we always had some,” Emilia says in the aftermath. So it
was decided that a sizeable stock of mayonnaise would always be maintained at the
Roswaal manor.]

[In the end, the plan to use mayonnaise to boost Rem’s self-confidence backfired
spectacularly. After this incident, Rem still bears a trauma toward mayonnaise. Despite
her genuine skill in making it, it ultimately fell to Ram to produce mayonnaise for the
manor.]

*

I didn't change much, but I did tone down Ram and Subaru's reactions to the mayo-bath
just a little bit. I couldn't see Ram shouting at her little sister with [unspeakable
violence] in basically any circumstances, nor could I see Subaru actively, GENUINELY
traumatizing Rem over something like this (or at least, not without bringing it up again
at some point as a guilty memory). I chalked up both of these inconsistencies to the fact
that they were some of the very first side stories written back when Tappei was early in
the Web Novel and everyone was a little bit...off, when compared to their final
personalities. I really changed very, very little, but I didn't want to Not Tell You. So
consider this your disclaimer.

Happy New Year!
